units.parent: NONE (peer of UBC/KIFS in the flywheel)

units.name: Universal Immunity Capital
units.text: Capital produced when a failure family is eliminated, protecting every future applicable mission with a reuse multiplier.

units.name: Universal Knowledge Runtime (UKR)
units.text: A pre-existing runtime already contemplating Self-Improving Agent Skills, promotion from repositories/datasets, and inheritance of validated patterns by future agents. Its Progressive Knowledge Loading and on-demand chapter/topic paging are reinforced with book-to-skill patterns.

units.name: Universal Learning Record
units.text: The abstracted, domain-agnostic counterpart to the Concrete Incident Dossier, describing the failure mechanism, violated invariant, preconditions, trigger pattern, applicable/non-applicable contexts, detection/prevention patterns, and UKDL/baseline/benchmark/mutation candidacy.

units.name: Universal Pattern Discovery
units.text: Many specific incidents can reveal a law no one wrote manually, e.g. multiple stale-state cases distilling to a caching invariant.
entities: REALITY-CRITICAL DECISIONS MUST NOT DEPEND ON UNVERIFIED CACHED ASSUMPTIONS

units.name: Universal Production Archetypes
units.text: Baseline families (UI Feature, API Integration, Persistent State, Migration, Agent, Background Worker, Plugin, CLI, Dataset Pipeline, Deployment, Security-Sensitive Mutation) each with adaptable defaults.

units.name: Universal Production Completion Standard
units.text: Feature completeness requires all applicable dimensions of correctness, integration, performance, observability, recoverability, versionability, compatibility, lifecycle, degradation, security, evidence, Production Reality, and institutional learning.

units.name: Universal Production System Evolution & Intelligence Platform
units.text: A universalized version of KSEIP (a KobiiCraft-specific system) that treats "software" as a full Production Estate (source, generated artifacts, effective configuration, dependencies, data, runtime state, infrastructure, deployment, external services, operator procedures, user-visible behavior) rather than just a repository, and learns how to produce, verify, operate, reconstruct, and evolve complete system instances with decreasing surprise and human intervention.
entities: Universal Production System Evolution & Intelligence Platform
units.parent: NONE (peer system, KSEIP is its KobiiCraft vertical)
units.canonical_key: universal production system evolution intelligence platform

units.name: Universalization Quality
units.text: Rewards UKDL entries that actually prevent failures, not merely entry count.

units.name: Universalization Tax
units.text: A mandatory obligation that every feature, on completion, must be asked what universal capabilities it financed for the rest of KME, so no feature stays a bespoke island.

units.name: Unknown-Bug Detector
units.text: If no known genome explains the evidence, mark it a novel failure class candidate — this is the frontier.

units.name: Validity-by-Accident Gate
units.text: An explicit pre-Done gate asking whether correctness is "by construction" or merely "by circumstance" (single provider, no restart yet, permissive fallback, favorable load order, etc.); dependence on non-contractual circumstance is flagged as Latent Risk without necessarily blocking.

units.name: Vault-Grows / UKDL-Compresses Relationship
units.text: The Vault should expand with evidence while UKDL compresses into fewer, stronger rules — opposite of an infinite wiki.

units.name: Watchdog Day Pattern
units.text: A real KME performance incident became a technical rule and defensive system; universalized as the standard incident-to-baseline pipeline.
entities: Incident → root cause → invariant → regression → detector → UKDL → baseline

units.name: Web Time Machine / Source Change Sentinels
units.text: Maintains successive snapshots of external sources to observe evolution (API added/removed, support changed, warnings, migrations, benchmarks changed) over time, not just current state; Source Change Sentinels proactively monitor high-value sources (release notes, docs, compatibility matrix, security notices) and trigger a Source Drift Event → impact graph → affected capabilities/projects → revalidation when something changes.
entities: Web Time Machine / Source Change Sentinels
units.canonical_key: web time machine source change sentinels

units.name: Zero Unclassified Material Failure at Session Close
units.text: No material failure observed during a session may disappear without a disposition (fixed+institutionalized / fixed local-only / deferred / invalid / blocked / unresolved).
entities: Zero Unclassified Material Failure at Session Close
units.canonical_key: zero unclassified material failure at session close

units.name: Mastery to Baseline Promotion Loop
units.text: The loop connecting the exam/benchmark system to the construction flywheel: an active exam reaching 100+mastery promotes a standard, all future constructions inherit it, and the old exam retires into the Regression Vault while a harder exam is generated.

units.name: Baseline Floors and Frontier Ceilings
units.text: The distinction between FLOOR (what every applicable construction must already know) and FRONTIER (the hardest thing KME is currently trying to learn); new builds start at the floor, not zero.

units.name: Baseline Ratchet Non-Regression Law
units.text: The invariant that once a capability reaches a baseline level, no new environment may silently accept a lower level; incompatibility must be explicitly flagged and resolved.

units.name: Baseline Versioning
units.text: The mechanism allowing a baseline standard to be explicitly superseded (e.g. B8 -> B9) or even REJECTED given new evidence, without allowing accidental drift.

units.name: Construction Constitution
units.text: The highest tier of promoted baseline: archetype-independent laws of KME itself (e.g. stage before destructive mutation, no silent BlockState/NBT loss, function before decorative filler).

units.name: Universal Completion Standard
units.text: The rule that when a mission discovers a new dimension of "Done" (e.g. realized walkability, not just a route plan), that dimension becomes mandatory for all future relevant constructions, not only the discovering feature.

units.name: Done-Gate Expansion Ratchet
units.text: The versioned growth of the definition of "Done" (geometry -> runtime persistence -> reference integrity), strengthening over time while remaining applicability-aware to avoid over-ceremony on small assets.

units.name: Failure Immunity Flywheel
units.text: The mirror loop to the excellence flywheel for defects: every real failure becomes a minimal reproducer, root cause, regression, and where applicable a universal rule and future baseline, so each error reduces the probability of its whole family recurring.

units.name: Error Classes Distillation
units.text: The requirement to extract an abstract failure class (e.g. Host/Child Exterior-Interior Interface Not Validated) from a specific incident, rather than only recording the specific fact, so future unrelated builds benefit from one build's bug.

units.name: Knowledge Upward Movement
units.text: The principle that learning must flow upward from instance to archetype to domain to universal knowledge whenever possible, never remaining trapped at a lower scope.

units.name: Universal Transfer Evaluator
units.text: A process that asks, for each new capability, what other problem classes share its underlying abstraction (e.g. an Event Socket as a "reserved semantic spatial interface" transfers to seasonal lobbies, player shops, expansion districts, runtime NPC areas).

units.name: Baseline Packages by Archetype
units.text: A set of named baseline bundles composed per archetype (e.g. LuckyArena = Universal + World + Competitive + Dynamic) so new constructions inherit a clean composition instead of a flat list.
entities: UNIVERSAL CORE / WORLD CORE / BUILDING CORE / SOCIAL CORE / COMPETITIVE CORE / DYNAMIC CORE

units.name: Certified Construction Primitives
units.text: Individually certified building-block capabilities (e.g. Entrance Interface B9, Terrain Foundation B8, BlockState Rotation B10) that new benchmarks can assume and build compositions on top of, rather than re-testing internals.

units.name: Baseline Caching
units.text: Reuse of previously evaluated motifs, calibrated thresholds, validated parameter ranges, and known performant materializations instead of recalculating them from scratch, reducing compute and latency.

units.name: Negative Knowledge Compounding
units.text: The complement of positive learning: recording what not to attempt again (e.g. naive radial topology everywhere, flatten terrain for every building) so it also compounds and reduces search.

units.name: Trap Registry
units.text: A registry of promoted failure patterns the planner consults before generating a candidate, since avoiding a bad strategy is cheaper than generating and repairing it.

units.name: Cheap Falsification Library
units.text: An accumulated library of cheap gates (silhouette, topology, capacity, fairness approximations, performance estimators) letting bad candidates be killed early, accelerating iteration.

units.name: Better-Baseline Cheaper-Search Feedback Loop
units.text: A positive feedback loop where better knowledge reduces bad candidates, lowering search cost, enabling more useful candidate exploration, raising result quality, and producing new high-quality patterns that feed back into better knowledge.
units.canonical_key: better baseline cheaper search feedback loop

units.name: Generator-Evaluator Coevolution Loop
units.text: A loop where a calibrated evaluator selects better candidates, which expose subtler failure cases, which further improve the evaluator, so generator and evaluator coevolve.

units.name: Flywheel Priority Oracle
units.text: A decision rule that, among multiple possible improvements, selects the one that raises the baseline of all of KME the most, preserving the compound effect.

units.name: Construction-derived R&D
units.text: The practice of treating every new map as an applied-research experiment (e.g. Cantina as a social-space laboratory, LuckyArena as a dynamic-state/fairness laboratory) rather than separating research from production.

units.name: Capability Curriculum through Production
units.text: Using the production roadmap itself as the capability-training curriculum by deliberately choosing missions that both deliver value and force a targeted KME weakness to be solved.

units.name: Multidimensional Technical Level
units.text: A definition of "technical level" split into six independent dimensions (generation quality, evaluation quality, verification quality, efficiency, experience, and transfer), each of which must be proven before a capability can baseline-promote.
entities: GENERATION LEVEL / EVALUATION LEVEL / REALITY LEVEL / PERFORMANCE LEVEL / UX LEVEL / GENERALIZATION LEVEL

units.name: Evidence Bundle
units.text: The required documentation package for every promoted baseline: source failures, goldens, benchmark results, adversarial results, scope, version, regressions, known exceptions.

units.name: Baseline Revocation
units.text: The mechanism for suspending a baseline that turns out to have a hidden failure, identifying affected systems, and issuing a fix version, preventing a flywheel-propagated error from spreading unchecked.

units.name: Blast Radius Awareness
units.text: The recognition that the same compounding effect that spreads excellence can spread bugs, so universal capabilities require stronger evidence before promotion proportional to their reuse.

units.name: Baseline Canary Set
units.text: A representative sample of construction types (lobby, arena, building, terrain, nested build, old-version artifact) tested before promoting a universal capability to surface cross-domain regressions.

units.name: Pareto Non-Regression Requirement
units.text: The requirement that a baseline promotion may not silently trade a large drop in one critical dimension (e.g. performance) for a gain in another (e.g. craftsmanship) without explicit evaluation.

units.name: Flywheel Metrics Dashboard
units.text: A conceptual dashboard of flywheel-health metrics: Baseline Height, Baseline Coverage, Reuse Multiplier, Time-to-Reference, Time-to-Production, First-Pass Quality, Regression Escape Rate, Universalization Rate, Search Waste, Capability Compound Rate.

units.name: Time-to-Excellence
units.text: The flagship metric measuring elapsed time from intent-accepted to reference-class-plus-Production-Reality result, expected to fall exponentially as Construction Memory grows.

units.name: First Excellent Candidate Rate
units.text: A metric measuring what fraction of first-pass candidates are already excellent, rising over time as evidence that KME is accumulating intelligence rather than brute-forcing quality.

units.name: Multilayer Excellence Compounding
units.text: The chain by which better representation improves planning, which improves candidates, which lets evaluators see subtler failures, which improves Goldens, which improves DNA, which improves generation — a flywheel across abstraction layers.

units.name: KME Master Flywheel Loop
units.text: The full closed loop of the KME flywheel: build/benchmark/incident -> observe -> root-cause -> distill -> classify scope -> implement/improve capability -> benchmark -> adversarial validate -> transfer validate -> production reality -> promote to baseline -> register golden path+traps+oracles -> propagate -> rebenchmark downstream -> discover emergent combinations -> raise frontier -> build harder things -> repeat.

units.name: Mastery Produces Both Floor and Ceiling
units.text: The unifying rule that reaching mastery (100) on a benchmark simultaneously raises the floor (capability becomes baseline) and raises the ceiling (a harder exam appears), permanently trapping the system between a rising floor and rising frontier.
entities: Mastery Produces Both Floor and Ceiling
units.canonical_key: mastery produces both floor and ceiling

units.name: KME Universal Capability Ratchet & Compounding Excellence Flywheel
units.text: The formal name proposed for the KME flywheel, composed of five conceptual subsystems: Capability Maturity Registry, Baseline Promotion & Inheritance Layer, Universal Knowledge Distillation Layer, Capability Propagation & Composition Miner, Adaptive Frontier Benchmark Controller.
entities: KME Universal Capability Ratchet & Compounding Excellence Flywheel
units.canonical_key: kme universal capability ratchet compounding excellence flywheel

units.name: KME Constitutional Principles
units.text: Five constitutional principles governing KME: every proven improvement must be considered for baseline promotion; every applicable construction must inherit the strongest proven baseline absent documented exception; every mastered benchmark raises floor and creates a harder frontier; every failure must increase permanent immunity or explain why not; no important construction should only improve the map, it should improve KME.

units.name: UCR-CIF Hard Postcondition
units.text: The postcondition defining when a reusable engineering delta counts as institutionalized: only once it demonstrably changes the starting conditions of future applicable work.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Construction Event
units.text: The fundamental unit of UCR-CIF: any sufficiently significant act of construction produced by Claude Code (feature, fix, refactor, migration, module, service, library, CLI, agent, hook, workflow, API, schema, runtime, test infra, benchmark, dataset, governance mechanism, deployment mechanism, etc.).
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Construction Intelligence Record
units.text: The rich record generated per Construction Event, capturing intent, project, mission, affected architecture, artifacts, interfaces, dependencies, invariants, capabilities used, baselines applied, tests, benchmarks, Production Reality evidence, incidents, failed approaches, trade-offs, decisions, reusable discoveries, lineage, provenance, confidence, evidence tier, and promotion candidates.

units.name: Host-Resident Construction Observer
units.text: A user-level-installed observer, not scoped to any single project, that watches Claude Code across the event surface (session/tool/write/edit/bash/tests/commits), repository surface (git status/diffs/commits/deps/config), verification surface (tests/lint/CI/deploy), and reality surface (crashes/rollback/incidents/corrections), so construction is captured even when CPP is not activated for a mission.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: CPP Project Activation vs Resident Institutional Kernel
units.text: The split between CPP Project Activation (a project opting into the full CPP agent/command/runtime suite) and the CPP Resident Institutional Kernel (a minimal, always-on component providing capture, identity, provenance, baseline lookup, critical enforcement, and writeback regardless of whether full CPP is present).
entities: CPP Project Activation vs Resident Institutional Kernel
units.canonical_key: cpp project activation vs resident institutional kernel

units.name: Resident Institutional Kernel Installation Contract
units.text: The requirement that the global CPP installer must explicitly and mandatorily install the Resident Institutional Kernel (not just opt-in assets), with health check, versioning, self-test, atomic upgrade, rollback, hook-registration verification, stale-install detection, drift detection, and fail-safe behavior, since universal capture cannot depend on someone remembering to copy a hook.
units.parent: CPP Project Activation vs Resident Institutional Kernel

units.name: Universal Construction Ledger
units.text: A new ledger, distinct from the existing Global Baseline Ledger, that answers what was built, what was learned, what capabilities were involved, and what changed institutionally as a result, supporting queries on origin, adoption, obsolescence, and unconsumed promotions.

units.name: Artifact plus Institutional Delta
units.text: The UCR-CIF restatement of the dual-output rule: every significant mission produces a local deliverable (Output A) and an institutional delta (Output B, possibly zero, but only after being explicitly analyzed).
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Universalization Tax (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The UCR-CIF restatement requiring every relevant construction, before closing, to answer what was discovered that could reduce future work and at what level it should live (LOCAL/PROJECT/STACK/LANGUAGE/ARCHETYPE/DOMAIN/CROSS-DOMAIN/PLATFORM/UNIVERSAL/CONSTITUTIONAL).

units.name: Capability Authority Registry (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The UCR-CIF registry answering, per problem class (spatial transformation, process recovery, persistent state, HTTP retry, secrets handling, CLI/frontend contract, atomic writes, schema migration, etc.), which is the strongest approved provider, preventing every project from reinventing the same abstraction.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Capability Baseline Graph
units.text: The recognition that baselines are not scalar: real maturity is multidimensional per capability (e.g. Testing B9, Observability B6, Crash Recovery B8, Security B10), so the true baseline state must be represented as a graph, not a single number.

units.name: Capability Contract
units.text: The mandatory schema for any promoted capability: Identity, Authority, Scope, Applicability predicate, Maturity, Evidence, Golden Path, Alternatives, Dependencies, Consumers, Regression suite, Known failures, Traps, Supersession, Migration policy, Blast radius.

units.name: Baseline Applicability Resolver
units.text: A resolver enforcing that every applicable baseline is mandatory but not every baseline applies to every artifact (e.g. Markdown docs don't need transactional migration; a disposable script doesn't inherit financial-system ceremony).

units.name: Baseline Capability Pack (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The compiled composition (Universal Core + Language Core + Runtime Core + Artifact-Type Core + Architecture Core + Reliability Tier + Security Tier + Domain Core + Project Core + Mission-Specific Requirements) automatically assembled before a mission begins, so the only remaining question is what is unique about this specific construction.

units.name: Baseline Compiler
units.text: The mechanism that compiles the Baseline Capability Pack rather than loading an encyclopedia into context: detect project reality -> classify construction -> resolve applicability -> traverse capability graph -> select strongest approved providers -> resolve conflicts -> eliminate irrelevant doctrine -> emit minimum sufficient baseline.

units.name: Baseline Promotion Gate (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The UCR-CIF promotion ladder (OBSERVED -> LOCAL SUCCESS -> REPEATED SUCCESS -> CROSS-CONTEXT -> CROSS-PROJECT -> ADVERSARIAL -> PRODUCTION REALITY -> REGRESSION PROOF -> TRANSFER PROOF -> PROMOTED), with required evidence scaling by reuse multiplier.

units.name: Pareto Promotion Gate
units.text: A gate preventing a capability from ascending to baseline if it improves one metric while silently destroying another (e.g. -30% latency but -50% reliability); promotion must be Pareto-preserving on critical dimensions (correctness, reliability, security, performance, operability, maintainability, complexity, cost, DX, portability) or must explicitly record the trade-off.

units.name: Baseline Inheritance Debt
units.text: The CPP name for excellence debt: exists when a mature institutional capability already solves a problem but a new construction uses an inferior implementation without justification (e.g. Atomic Persistence B9 exists, new subsystem implements Persistence B3).

units.name: Authority Bypass Detector
units.text: A detector for duplicate lower-quality implementations, stale providers, copied old patterns, local reinvention, bypass of a common primitive, ignoring an institutional wrapper, old evaluators, obsolete recovery paths, weaker security handling, or legacy test strategy.

units.name: Golden Paths (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The default recommended mechanism per mature capability; alternatives remain valid but departing from the Golden Path requires justification, not the Golden Path itself, collapsing the decision search space.

units.name: Certified Engineering Primitives
units.text: Sufficiently mature capabilities certified as reusable primitives (atomic file writer, process supervisor, retry policy, structured logging contract, repository resolver, resilient subprocess execution, transaction wrapper, rollback primitive, test harness, configuration loader, state snapshot primitive) that new features need not re-verify internally, only in composition.

units.name: Composition Intelligence
units.text: The mechanism by which improving one capability triggers re-evaluation of dependent capabilities, some combinations crossing a new threshold and yielding an emergent superior capability that was never explicitly designed (e.g. durable state + crash recovery + session identity + process reattachment + checkpoint consistency -> Durable Execution Continuity).

units.name: Cross-Domain Transfer (UCR-CIF)
units.text: Transfer of a solution by causal/structural abstraction rather than by name (e.g. Orca's crash-safe session restoration structurally transfers to agent recovery, background jobs, build pipelines, distributed workflows; KME's exact rollback transfers to database migrations, config changes, deployment experiments).

units.name: Negative Knowledge Flywheel
units.text: The UCR-CIF version of negative-knowledge accumulation: every construction also produces knowledge about what not to do again, feeding Universal Traps, Domain Traps, failure genomes, search priors, architecture rejectors, and cheap falsification gates.

units.name: Search Space Collapse (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The narrowing from ~100 plausible strategies for a new problem class down to a handful of context-conditioned Golden Paths as institutional evidence accumulates, driving a feedback loop of less search waste, more useful exploration, better candidates, subtler discovered failures, and better knowledge.

units.name: Failure Immunity Ratchet
units.text: The UCR-CIF failure pipeline: FAILURE -> evidence capture -> minimal reproducer -> root cause -> failure class -> causal abstraction -> exposure search -> regression -> preventive capability -> baseline candidate -> cross-project sweep; reframes "did we fix the bug" as "did we immunize the institution against this bug family".

units.name: Future-Project Immunity Test
units.text: The definitive test of true institutionalization: a failure discovered today in one project (e.g. Orca) must automatically benefit a project created six months later, without that project's team knowing about the incident, reading it, or being reminded.

units.name: Completion Standard Ratchet
units.text: The versioned growth of the Definition of Done as new dimensions are discovered (tests pass -> integration reachability -> persistence verification -> recovery proof), becoming progressively smarter, not merely longer.

units.name: Ratchet-on-Touch (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The UCR-CIF migration policy: new work must meet current baseline, old work upgrades on touch, except when a baseline is security-critical, data-loss-critical, corruption-critical, recovery-critical, or production-critical, which forces immediate migration.

units.name: Universal Construction Bootstrap
units.text: The guarantee that even in a brand-new repo/stack unknown to Claude Power Pack, the Resident Kernel automatically supplies engineering constitution, evidence discipline, state correctness, error handling baseline, test integrity, security floor, repository hygiene, observability floor, reality contract, rollback requirements, lifecycle integrity, completion proof, and institutional capture before project-specific intelligence is layered on top.

units.name: Institutional Sensor Function
units.text: The dual role every repo built with Claude Code acquires: its Product Function (building its own product) and its Institutional Sensor Function (discovering limitations, patterns, failures, capabilities, abstractions, missing baselines, better tools/architectures/evaluators) so any repo, however small, can improve Claude Power Pack.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Existing-System Compounding Retrofit
units.text: A mandatory initial sweep over everything that already exists (modules, tools, hooks, commands, agents, skills, governance, UKDL, datasets, tests, benchmarks, incidents, ledgers, architecture docs, historical learnings) asking what capabilities exist but aren't registered as authority, what learnings are documented but not compiled, what tests represent implicit capabilities, what baselines are written but not enforced, so the past also starts compounding interest.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Existing Systems as Flywheel Stations
units.text: The principle that UCR-CIF does not replace existing CPP systems (Universal Knowledge Runtime, Cognitive Capital Fabric, ULTEF, ICAF, IRCF, failure systems, SQI, Evidence-First Architecture, Autonomous Integrity & Self-Healing, Autoresearch, Software Evolution Intelligence, Knowledge Sovereignty, Capability Runtime, UKDL, Production Reality Gate, Universal Quality & Iteration Intelligence) but turns them into stations of one circuit that feed each other.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: CPP Master Flywheel Loop
units.text: The full UCR-CIF loop: mission -> compile best-known baseline -> build -> observe construction -> verify reality -> capture construction record -> detect deltas -> root-cause failures -> extract reusable capabilities -> classify applicability -> compare against existing authorities -> reuse/extend/supersede/reject -> promotion gate -> update capability graph -> update golden paths -> update tests/oracles/traps -> propagate -> rebenchmark dependents -> detect emergent compositions -> raise baseline -> raise frontier -> next mission starts higher.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Mastery Elevates Floor and Ceiling (CPP)
units.text: The CPP restatement that a mastered capability simultaneously produces a higher baseline (floor) and generates a next, harder frontier (ceiling), trapping CPP between a non-degradable floor and an ever-advancing frontier.
units.canonical_key: mastery elevates floor and ceiling cpp

units.name: Benchmark Retirement
units.text: The rule that a fully-mastered benchmark does not disappear but moves to the Regression Vault while a harder benchmark is created above it, preserving the floor while expanding the ceiling.

units.name: Systemic Leverage Score (UCR-CIF)
units.text: A prioritization score for improvements based on number of consumers, number of exposed projects, frequency of use, current weakness, failure recurrence, cost/time avoided, reliability/quality uplift, generalization potential, composition potential, blast radius, and difficulty.

units.name: Reuse Multiplier (UCR-CIF)
units.text: A count of how many later constructions used a given capability; a small improvement with RM 500 can be institutionally more valuable than a large single-use feature.

units.name: Baseline Coverage (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The percentage of a new construction already resolved by mature capabilities before new work starts, expected to rise from ~20% toward ~90% over institutional time, freeing iteration budget for genuinely new problems.

units.name: Time To Production Excellence
units.text: The flagship UCR-CIF metric: elapsed time from intent-accepted to a production-real, verified, reference-grade deliverable, expected to fall as institutional intelligence increases.

units.name: First-Pass Excellence Rate
units.text: A metric measuring what percentage of new constructions pass their strong gates on the first serious implementation attempt, rising if knowledge is truly compounding and flat if only documentation is accumulating.

units.name: Human Rediscovery Rate
units.text: A metric counting how many times the Owner has to say "we already learned this," with a target of zero, framed as one of the most important CPP metrics.

units.name: Baseline Escape Rate
units.text: A metric counting how often a new system manages to introduce an inferior implementation than an existing authority without being detected, target zero.

units.name: Institutionalization Closure Rate
units.text: The percentage of promoted learnings that are actually consumed by future work; a stored-but-unconsumed learning does not count as a closed flywheel.

units.name: Verification Amortization
units.text: The property that a certified capability lets most of its evidence be reused rather than re-certified from scratch — only composition needs re-verification — so growing robustness need not imply indefinitely growing cost.

units.name: Capability Compound Rate
units.text: A metric measuring how much downstream capability rises when a primitive improves (e.g. Atomic State B6->B9 improving recovery, rollback, session continuity, migrations, agent persistence, deployment state, experimentation).

units.name: Baseline Cache (UCR-CIF)
units.text: A reuse cache of validated providers, calibrated thresholds, proven configurations, verified algorithms, known safe ranges, benchmark Goldens, test fixtures, failure reproducers, observability schemas, and compatibility matrices, avoiding re-investigating the already-proven.

units.name: Change Blast Radius
units.text: The requirement that a modification to a universal capability needs a regression surface proportional to its fanout — local utility needs local tests, a global persistence primitive needs a large cross-project canary set.

units.name: Universal Canary Portfolio
units.text: A representative portfolio (CLI, frontend, backend, stateful service, agent system, plugin, old repository, Windows, POSIX, small project, large monorepo) against which high-fanout capabilities are tested to demonstrate real transfer before universal promotion.

units.name: Capability Dependency Graph (UCR-CIF)
units.text: A graph of capability dependencies (e.g. Durable Agent Recovery depends on State Snapshot, Session Identity, Process Supervision, Persistence Integrity, Recovery Verification, Failure Detection) so that a local improvement triggers reevaluation of all downstream dependents.

units.name: Baseline Propagation (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The pipeline from a capability improving through dependency-graph query, affected-consumer identification, risk classification, rebenchmarking representative consumers, migration candidates, new composed baselines, to frontier discovery, without requiring every repo to be modified automatically.

units.name: New Construction Bootstrap (UCR-CIF)
units.text: The revised construction-start sequence under UCR-CIF: project reality detected -> construction classified -> capabilities resolved -> best known baseline compiled -> negative knowledge injected -> golden paths available -> known traps excluded -> certified primitives reused -> only true novelty remains, replacing from-scratch investigation.

units.name: Universal Construction Constitution
units.text: The highest-tier universal laws that mature CPP capabilities can ascend to (e.g. preserve intent across representations, no destructive mutation without proportional recoverability, no Done without appropriate evidence, no duplicated weaker implementation when a stronger authority exists, no operational feature without an observable trigger-to-effect path).

units.name: Knowledge Decay Detection
units.text: A check asking not just "did this work" but "is this still true," particularly for frameworks, APIs, runtimes, security, performance, platforms, model capabilities, and agent harnesses, preventing an old baseline from becoming dogma.

units.name: UCR-CIF Constitutional Laws UC-01 through UC-15
units.text: The fifteen named constitutional laws of UCR-CIF governing teaching, baseline inheritance, non-regression, authority-before-reinvention, dual output, evidence-before-promotion, applicability, evidence-proportional-to-reuse, failure immunity, mastery, knowledge-must-change-behavior, negative knowledge compounding, composition-before-new-system, host-level capture, and no-human-rediscovery.
entities: UCR-CIF Constitutional Laws UC-01 through UC-15
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric
units.canonical_key: ucr cif constitutional laws uc 01 through uc 15

units.name: UCR-CIF Relation to ULTEF
units.text: The defined boundary where ULTEF converts experience into institutional knowledge (learning -> truth -> generalization -> institutional form) while UCR-CIF turns the whole construction cycle into a machine that generates, consumes, and elevates that knowledge continuously, feeding back into ULTEF.

units.name: UCR-CIF Relation to IRCF
units.text: IRCF is defined as the institution (governing doctrine, evidence, promotion, cross-project intelligence, institutional yield, evolution); UCR-CIF is one of its fundamental economic circuits, turning every construction into continuous flow through those authorities.

units.name: UCR-CIF Relation to Cognitive Capital Fabric
units.text: CCF avoids re-paying for understanding; UCR-CIF avoids re-paying for discovering how to build correctly; together they produce understanding compounding plus engineering compounding.
entities: UCR-CIF Relation to Cognitive Capital Fabric
units.canonical_key: ucr cif relation to cognitive capital fabric

units.name: UCR-CIF Relation to Autoresearch
units.text: UCR-CIF produces the frontier (capability X, current floor, unknown ceiling, highest systemic leverage) that Autoresearch investigates; discoveries pass through ULTEF (transmute) and ICAF (ascend) before UCR-CIF converts them into a new starting point, pulling external research into the compounding loop.

units.name: Network of Flywheels
units.text: The recognition that the end result is not one flywheel but a network of connected flywheels (Construction, Failure Immunity, Research, Quality, Knowledge, Capability, Architecture, Observability, Testing, Recovery, Cost, Agent, Dataset) all exchanging improvements via the shared Capability Graph and Construction Ledger.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Global Institutional Backfill
units.text: The first operation to run after building UCR-CIF: mine existing CPP doctrine (rather than write new doctrine) into capabilities, authorities, dependencies, applicability rules, Goldens, benchmarks, traps, failure classes, evidence bundles, certified primitives, completion gates, and composition opportunities, turning existing stock into circulating capital.

units.name: UCR-CIF Build Order
units.text: The prescribed build sequence: P0 Host-Resident Construction Observer, Universal Construction Ledger, Capability Authority Registry, Baseline Applicability Compiler; P1 Construction Delta Miner, ICAF/ULTEF Bridge, Baseline Inheritance Gate, Existing-System Backfill; P2 Dependency & Propagation Graph, Composition Opportunity Miner, Frontier Controller; P3 Institutional Economics.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: UCR-CIF Constitutional Formulation
units.text: The definitive constitutional laws of UCR-CIF: every construction must begin from the strongest applicable proven baseline; every significant construction must be observed as a potential source of reusable capital; every proven reusable delta must be connected to the capability graph or explicitly rejected; every failure must increase immunity or produce an explicit non-generalization verdict; every mastered capability must raise the floor and expose a higher frontier; no new construction may silently reintroduce an inferior known-solvable solution; CPP activation may deepen intelligence but must not gate whether experience is captured.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric
units.text: The second-order evolution of UCR-CIF: instead of only accumulating improvements, it continuously improves the machinery that discovers improvements, and then improves the machinery that improves that machinery — the system must compound not only capability but its own rate of capability acquisition.
entities: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric
units.canonical_key: claude power pack recursive compounding intelligence engineering acceleration fabric

units.name: Three Orders of Compounding
units.text: A taxonomy distinguishing reuse of a single improvement (first-order), improvement of the capacity to discover improvements such as a better evaluator (second-order), and improvement of the mechanisms that decide what to improve (third-order) — the real leap in leverage.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric

units.name: Meta-Ratchet
units.text: A ratchet above the Capability Ratchet that maintains baselines for the quality of distillation, benchmark generation, transfer detection, root-cause analysis, applicability classification, capability composition, search-space pruning, R&D prioritization, Production Reality verification, and institutionalization itself.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric

units.name: Learning Efficiency Baseline
units.text: A constitutional capability measuring how much reusable intelligence is obtained per construction, how much evidence is lost, how many correct abstractions are detected, how long promotion takes, and how many false generalizations occur.

units.name: Institutional Learning Yield
units.text: A metric measuring reusable value obtained per unit of work performed, not documents produced, distinguishing e.g. Artifact Value=1/Institutional Value=20 features from Artifact Value=10/Institutional Value=0.2 ones, changing roadmap prioritization.

units.name: Engineering Interest Rate
units.text: The deepest metric: how much future work is avoided or improved per unit of engineering done today; a primitive costing 10 hours that later saves 1,000 hours has an enormous EIR, and CPP should maximize such investments.

units.name: Improvement Derivatives
units.text: Improvements whose value derives from raising the productivity of many other improvements (a better evaluator, benchmark generator, repository-understanding engine, causal debugger, or applicability solver), warranting extraordinary priority because they improve the factory that produces improvements.

units.name: Transitive Systemic Leverage
units.text: A leverage measure counting not just direct consumers of a capability but transitive consumers of things that depend on it — a foundational capability may have 20 direct consumers but 800 transitive ones, its real value near 800.

units.name: Institutional Leverage Graph
units.text: The evolution of the Capability Graph into a graph over capabilities, primitives, agents, evaluators, benchmarks, datasets, architectures, workflows, hooks, tests, failure classes, knowledge, policies, and projects, with edges like depends-on/improves/constrains/validates/generates/consumes/supersedes/detects/protects/accelerates, enabling institution-wide impact calculation.

units.name: Improvement Propagation Simulator
units.text: A pre-investment simulation asking, if capability X improves, which direct and downstream consumers improve, which bottlenecks become dominant, and what new capabilities might emerge, allowing prioritization by expected compound effect.

units.name: Counterfactual Capability Mining
units.text: A post-construction question asking how a mission would have changed had capability X existed from the start, identifying avoidable bottlenecks, missing primitives/baselines/automation/knowledge/observability.

units.name: Friction Mining
units.text: Treats every human intervention (reminding a requirement, correcting architecture, repeating a rule, discovering a bug, insisting on Production Reality) as a sensor, recorded as an Institutional Friction Event asking why the institution needed the intervention.

units.name: Human Intervention Burden
units.text: A metric targeting zero for repetitive categories of human intervention (reminders, policing, rediscovery, repetitive verification, repeated debugging, repeated architecture corrections), while preserving decisions that genuinely require human judgment.

units.name: Owner Correction Mining
units.text: A classification pipeline for every Owner correction ("this should have been done this way") into LOCAL/PREFERENCE/PROJECT RULE/DOMAIN RULE/UNIVERSAL ENGINEERING RULE, attempting institutionalization when reusable.

units.name: Zero-Rediscovery Architecture
units.text: The ideal that once CPP has cognitively paid to solve something (research, debugging, architecture, benchmarking, experimentation, evaluation, tooling, infrastructure), that cost should not be fully paid again.

units.name: Solution Half-Life
units.text: A measure of how long an authority remains optimal, tracked via freshness, evidence age, dependency age, ecosystem compatibility, and performance relevance, guarding against institutional fossilization from compounding without renewal.

units.name: Continuous Authority Competition
units.text: The rule that the Authority Registry never permanently crowns an implementation; candidates can compete against the current authority and win per-context or supersede it entirely once a benchmark suite demonstrates superiority.

units.name: Capability Tournament
units.text: A structured comparison for important capabilities of the current Golden Path against new implementations, alternative architectures, external techniques, and synthesized approaches across correctness, reliability, performance, maintainability, simplicity, cost, and portability, preventing baseline stagnation.

units.name: Automatic Challenger Generation
units.text: When an authority matures too comfortably, CPP asks what an alternative would need to do to defeat it and builds a challenger benchmark, applying continuous evolutionary pressure even to the best systems.

units.name: Institutional Natural Selection
units.text: A pipeline (variation -> benchmark -> reality -> competition -> selection -> promotion -> reuse) ensuring the best solutions win by evidence, never by age, documentation volume, or authorship.

units.name: Architecture Evolution Engine
units.text: A process that detects when several local capabilities converge on a common unnamed superior architecture primitive (e.g. several projects independently implementing event capture, durable state, provenance, rollback, recovery) and validates it as a reusable substrate.

units.name: Architecture Compression
units.text: The rule that with sufficient evidence, five patterns become a primitive, ten primitives a subsystem, five subsystems a platform capability, reducing conceptual complexity — the institution must compress what it learns, not just grow by addition.

units.name: Complexity Deflation
units.text: A metric counting how many new decisions a typical construction requires, which must fall over time if compounding is well-designed; badly-designed compounding instead produces more systems, rules, files, and orchestration.

units.name: Knowledge Compiler
units.text: The mechanism ensuring Construction Memory is compiled, not injected directly: mission -> detect needs -> resolve capabilities -> resolve current authorities -> retrieve relevant traps -> retrieve critical evidence -> emit minimal operational context, maximizing institutional knowledge while minimizing context burden.

units.name: Context ROI Ratchet
units.text: A rule that every unit of token/context consumed should justify decision impact, risk reduction, or quality uplift; CPP must learn which knowledge actually changes outcomes and exclude the rest from active context.

units.name: Context Outcome Attribution
units.text: A post-mission analysis of which retrieved knowledge actually influenced the outcome, which was ignored, and what knowledge was missing, so the next project's retrieval improves — knowledge retrieval itself learns from every construction.

units.name: Capability Consumption Telemetry
units.text: Telemetry tracking when a capability was offered, used, rejected, improved the result, or created problems, distinguishing an admired capability from a productive one.

units.name: Dead Knowledge Detection
units.text: Detection of knowledge with zero retrieval, zero consumers, and zero outcome impact, flagged as possibly too specific, poorly indexed, obsolete, duplicated, or useless — the flywheel also needs pruning.

units.name: Institutional Garbage Collection
units.text: The pruning process eliminating or archiving duplicated rules, superseded patterns, dead benchmarks, unused abstractions, obsolete providers, and conflicting docs — compounding requires accumulation plus compression plus selection plus deletion.

units.name: Autonomous Frontier Discovery
units.text: A process by which CPP does not wait for a project to reveal weaknesses but asks which part of the capability graph currently limits the most downstream value, making that node the new frontier.

units.name: Bottleneck Cascades
units.text: The loop where solving bottleneck A reveals bottleneck B: A solved -> recompute graph -> B becomes dominant -> attack B -> recompute, keeping the improvement portfolio always following the true frontier.

units.name: Constraint-First R&D
units.text: A research-prioritization rule to investigate constraints that block multiple downstream capabilities rather than merely "interesting things."

units.name: Autonomous R&D Portfolio
units.text: A conceptual portfolio of R&D categories CPP maintains: Exploitation (improve known capabilities), Exploration (new paradigms), Reliability (eliminate dangerous failure classes), Infrastructure (foundational primitives), Metrology (better evaluators), Compression (simplify existing systems), Frontier (solve still-impossible capabilities).

units.name: Portfolio Allocation by Expected Institutional Return
units.text: A prioritization scheme scoring each candidate improvement by expected leverage, confidence, evidence cost, implementation cost, blast radius, reversibility, and strategic unlocks, ranked by Expected Institutional Return.
entities: Portfolio Allocation by Expected Institutional Return
units.canonical_key: portfolio allocation by expected institutional return

units.name: Cheap Experiments First
units.text: A discipline of running cheap uncertainty-reducing experiments before committing to expensive implementation — buying cheap information before expensive implementation.
units.parent: Portfolio Allocation by Expected Institutional Return

units.name: Value of Information
units.text: A metric recognizing that research can be valuable even without producing a feature, e.g. by eliminating a bad architecture before weeks of investment.

units.name: Autonomous Experiment Factory
units.text: A pipeline for strategic capabilities: hypothesis -> minimal experiment -> benchmark -> evidence -> decision, so production is not the first place ideas are tested.

units.name: Synthetic Adversarial Worlds
units.text: Purpose-built causal adversarial environments generated per capability to break it, asking what condition would falsify its assumptions and constructing that condition, rather than relying only on random testing.

units.name: Failure Frontier Generator
units.text: A generator that, given an evaluator's currently detectable failure classes (A-B-C), produces harder failure class D to expose it, then E once D is caught, driving continuous evaluator evolution.

units.name: Metrology Before Optimization
units.text: The rule that CPP must not optimize dimensions it measures poorly, since many architectures appear to improve only because their evaluator is weak.

units.name: Evaluator Confidence
units.text: A declared profile per evaluator of coverage, false positives, false negatives, calibration, and known blind spots, so a score is never mistaken for truth.

units.name: Reality Arbitrates
units.text: The rule that when a benchmark says PASS but production says FAIL, the benchmark loses authority and a Metrology Incident is automatically created, not just a product bug.

units.name: Benchmark Genome
units.text: The ancestry record of a benchmark: what failure created it, what capability it measures, what blind spots it corrected, what versions it superseded — benchmarks also accumulate intelligence.

units.name: Benchmark Synthesis
units.text: Combining failures from different projects (e.g. race condition from A + persistence failure from B + network loss from C) into a new adversarial benchmark harder than any of the originals.

units.name: Cross-Project Adversarial Recombination
units.text: A further compounding level where failure modes, not just solutions, are recombined, so a new system is tested against the combined memory of many failure classes.

units.name: Failure Genome Library
units.text: A registry describing every failure class causally (trigger, hidden assumption, violated invariant, propagation mechanism, observable symptoms, detection opportunity, prevention mechanism) rather than as a bare incident name, enabling cross-stack transfer.

units.name: Capability Recombination
units.text: Deliberate recombination of capabilities (A+B, A+C, B+D, A+B+E) searching for emergent problem classes, turning the capability graph into an invention space.

units.name: Recombination Yield
units.text: A metric counting how many new capabilities were created via composition of existing ones, expected to rise as institutional wealth grows the space of useful combinations.

units.name: Capability Network Effects
units.text: The recognition that a capability's value is not additive: an isolated capability is worth X, but one connected to twenty others can be worth much more.

units.name: Interface Standardization as Accelerator
units.text: The requirement that capabilities share common contracts, evidence schemas, lifecycle, observability, and provenance so recombination stays cheap.

units.name: Composability Score
units.text: A metric of how many other capabilities a given one can reasonably integrate with, flagging highly composable capabilities for special attention.

units.name: Institutional Capability Liquidity
units.text: A measure of how easily a capability can be discovered, applied, and integrated (clear interface, evidence, multi-context, low integration cost); reusable-but-hard-to-consume knowledge has little compound effect.

units.name: Capability Economy
units.text: The framing of the whole system as a technical economy: projects produce capabilities, capabilities get reused, evidence determines trust, consumers generate feedback, better capabilities gain authority, obsolete ones lose consumption, and R&D invests where return is highest.
entities: From Knowledge Graph to Capability Economy

units.name: Compounding Across Projects
units.text: The principle that each project contributes something different (KME: generation/evaluation; Orca: durability/recovery; KobiiCraft: hardware/reality/debugging; a SaaS: deployment/observability; a CLI: DX/tooling) and UCR-CIF must find what each can learn from all others regardless of surface domain.

units.name: Cross-Language Transfer
units.text: The process of abstracting an improvement discovered in one language (e.g. Python) into an abstract principle, then providing it via Rust, TypeScript, or Go providers, so knowledge survives the language.

units.name: Cross-Runtime Transfer
units.text: Transfer of solutions across runtime contexts (desktop->server, CLI->agent, single-process->distributed) whenever the underlying causal abstraction is genuinely shared.

units.name: Universal Pattern Families
units.text: A small set of named pattern families (lifecycle integrity, state integrity, transactional safety, boundary validation, authority resolution, observability, recovery, orchestration, synchronization, identity, provenance) replacing thousands of isolated patterns, enabling extreme transferability.

units.name: Pattern-to-Primitive Ascension
units.text: The rule that a pattern family with enough evidence is converted into a reusable primitive, and enough primitives forming a unit become a platform capability, materializing the institution's best ideas.

units.name: Institutional Autofactoring
units.text: A process triggered when a better primitive appears, searching for old duplications that could be consolidated, prioritized by ROI and risk rather than executed blindly.

units.name: Ratchet-on-Relevance
units.text: A stronger alternative to Ratchet-on-Touch: when an important capability changes, compute which projects have enough relevance/risk to justify migration without waiting for the repo to be touched.

units.name: Compounding Migration Intelligence
units.text: The accumulation of migration knowledge (cost, breakages, compatibility issues, successful strategy) so each similar future migration becomes cheaper, eventually knowing which migrations tend to fail, what order works, what canaries are needed, and what rollback to use.

units.name: Institutional Replay
units.text: A verification method that takes historical missions and simulates how the current baseline would resolve them, comparing against the historical baseline's actual result to check whether CPP is truly improving.

units.name: Time-Machine Evaluation
units.text: A retrospective question: if current CPP had existed N months ago, how many bugs would it have avoided, how much work saved, what architecture would have changed, and what human interventions eliminated — measuring compounding with historical evidence.

units.name: Improvement Attribution
units.text: A requirement to attribute why a metric like TTPE fell (better model, better CPP, easier tasks, more compute), since without attribution one may falsely believe the flywheel is working.

units.name: Institutional A/B Testing
units.text: When safe, comparing baseline A vs baseline B on equivalent missions to obtain evidence on which institutional architecture produces better outcomes.

units.name: CPP as Experimental Subject
units.text: The fundamental rule that Claude Power Pack's own hooks, agents, commands, orchestrators, datasets, retrieval, governance, and evaluators are not exempt from the system: they too generate Construction Events, pay the Universalization Tax, undergo benchmarks, and can be superseded.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Construction Ratchet & Compounding Intelligence Fabric

units.name: No Sacred Subsystems
units.text: The rule that no component of Claude Power Pack is exempt from evidence-based replacement, even a constitutional piece, since the constitution protects principles, not implementations.

units.name: Self-Hosting Compounding
units.text: The eventual state where CPP uses CPP to improve CPP, under isolation, provenance, regression, rollback, and human governance for critical changes, so each CPP improvement increases the capacity to produce the next CPP improvement.

units.name: Recursive Institutional Yield
units.text: A named effect where improvement A accelerates discovery of B, which accelerates C, which improves capability extraction, so D, E, F produce more reusable intelligence than they otherwise would.

units.name: Improvement Chain Attribution
units.text: A record kept in Construction Memory of causal improvement chains (A enabled B, B accelerated C, C discovered D, D improved A) enabling identification of real positive feedback loops.

units.name: Positive Loop Miner
units.text: A search for cycles (A improves B, B improves C, C improves A) in the improvement chain, prioritizing healthy cycles since small investments can traverse them repeatedly.

units.name: Flywheel Amplification Score
units.text: A score for each possible improvement based on how many positive loops it feeds into, more loops meaning greater amplification potential.

units.name: Negative Feedback Detection
units.text: Detection of harmful compounding patterns, e.g. more tests -> higher latency -> less experimentation -> less learning, or more rules -> more context -> worse reasoning.

units.name: Anti-Bureaucracy Ratchet
units.text: A hard rule requiring institutional maturity to reduce net cognitive and execution burden, not merely add governance; a baseline that adds repetitive cost without sufficient return must be simplified.

units.name: Ceremony Budget
units.text: A budget requiring every institutional requirement's time/compute/context/complexity cost to be justified, preventing CPP from becoming a bureaucracy machine.

units.name: Progressive Proof Compression
units.text: The technique of representing an enormous evidence history via a certificate, authority, version, confidence, and compact evidence pointer, rather than re-injecting the full history.

units.name: Institutional Certificates
units.text: Certificates awarded to mature capabilities letting planners trust certain properties without continually re-proving internals.

units.name: Dynamic Trust
units.text: The rule that certificate trust is not permanent — it depends on version, environment, dependency changes, age, and incident history, maintaining reuse without complacency.

units.name: Global Construction Stream
units.text: The stream the Resident Institutional Kernel must maintain to fulfill "everything Claude Code builds from now on," feeding relevant events through local buffer -> provenance -> global ledger -> institutional analysis even outside CPP-enabled projects.

units.name: Offline-First Capture
units.text: The guarantee that if full CPP is unavailable, the event is still captured locally and reconciled later, so institutional memory never depends on connectivity or activation.

units.name: Exactly-Once Institutionalization Semantics
units.text: A requirement that Construction Events carry stable identity, deduplication, lineage, commit relationship, and merge semantics, preventing the same session from being registered multiple times.

units.name: Causal Construction Graph
units.text: A graph richer than a timeline: prompt -> decision -> edit -> test -> failure -> correction -> commit -> production result, enabling discovery of which actions caused which outcomes.

units.name: Learning From Successful Silence
units.text: The practice of analyzing not just failures but successes ("this worked perfectly the first time") to ask why, validating which baseline was decisive.

units.name: Baseline Contribution Attribution
units.text: Per-successful-mission attribution of which capabilities contributed value, revealing which ones truly raise first-pass quality.

units.name: Institutional Marginal Utility
units.text: The principle that prioritization should weigh marginal return, not just historical importance, since a heavily-used capability may be saturated while a new one could unlock much more.

units.name: Saturation Detector
units.text: A check asking whether continued investment in capability X still yields sufficient uplift; if not, investment moves to the new bottleneck, avoiding infinite local optimization.

units.name: Dynamic Frontier Allocation
units.text: The rule that CPP distributes effort where expected marginal institutional gain is maximal, not where the system has the most tradition/history.

units.name: Capability Option Value
units.text: A valuation recognizing capabilities that have little current use but enable many future possibilities (e.g. a generic durable execution substrate unlocking future autonomous workflows), which must be counted.

units.name: Unlock Graph
units.text: A graph tracking which capabilities a given capability could unlock (X unlocks Y, Z, Q), raising X's strategic priority even with few current consumers.

units.name: Architectural Moonshots
units.text: A small deliberate portion of the R&D portfolio reserved for high-uncertainty, high-potential, enormous-unlock-graph capabilities, without letting them absorb the whole budget.

units.name: Exploration Budget
units.text: An explicit budget for questioning dominant architectures, existing authorities, assumptions, and representations, without which CPP would converge too early on local maxima.

units.name: Representation Revolution Detector
units.text: A detector recognizing that many large improvements come from changing how a problem is represented rather than optimizing an algorithm, looking for many failures sharing a common representation limitation as a signal for a new abstraction layer.

units.name: Representation Leverage
units.text: The observation that a new representation can simultaneously improve planning, generation, testing, debugging, observability, and transfer — extraordinary-leverage improvements.

units.name: Fundamental Layer Priority
units.text: The rule that when choosing between a superficial feature improvement and a foundational representation defect with wide fanout, CPP must recognize the latter as the probable better institutional investment.

units.name: Autonomous Curriculum
units.text: The evolution of production-as-curriculum into a deliberately designed curriculum: if the capability graph shows a strategic weakness, missions or benchmarks are chosen to exercise it.

units.name: Curriculum Sequencing
units.text: A required sequencing of foundational prerequisite -> intermediate capability -> composition -> production validation -> frontier, rather than attacking arbitrary challenges, to accelerate mastery.

units.name: Difficulty Calibration
units.text: The requirement that CPP learn to generate benchmarks near the current frontier — neither too easy nor impossible — that maximize information gained.

units.name: Learning Progress Maximization
units.text: An R&D prioritization criterion valuing expected learning progress, not just final score, avoiding months spent on a still-premature frontier.

units.name: Failure Information Density
units.text: A prioritization criterion valuing failures that reveal many broken assumptions, i.e. high cross-system explanatory power.

units.name: Generalization Pressure
units.text: The discipline of preferring more general abstractions only when evidence supports them, never generalizing for elegance but for demonstrated predictive power.

units.name: Prediction Gate
units.text: A higher tier of evidence: a reusable theory gains major confidence when it correctly predicts a future failure it had not yet observed.

units.name: Predictive Institutional Knowledge
units.text: A reframing of the institutional-knowledge goal from remembering bugs to predicting where they will appear.

units.name: Risk Forecasting
units.text: The combination of Capability Graph, Failure Genome, and Project Genome to detect that a new subsystem combines risk factors historically producing e.g. state-loss failures, increasing verification before the incident occurs — converting reactive immunity into predictive immunity.

units.name: Prevention ROI
units.text: A conceptually fundamental but hard-to-measure metric attributing value to prevented incidents — the best failure is the one that never occurs.

units.name: Institutional Early Warning System
units.text: Pre-Done detection of architectural drift, baseline bypass, unusual complexity, duplicated capability, missing observability, weak test surface, and unresolved uncertainty.

units.name: Construction Risk Prior
units.text: A history-based prior of probable risks a mission starts with, treated as a prior rather than a rigid rule, reducing surprises.

units.name: Experience Curves per Problem Class
units.text: A measurement of how much TTPE falls after each exposure to a given problem class; if it doesn't fall, knowledge is not truly compounding — the learning curve becomes an institutional observable.

units.name: Plateau Detection
units.text: A check triggered when TTPE fails to improve after five missions of a class, asking whether knowledge capture, transfer, authority clarity, benchmark strength, context-specificity, or tooling is the bottleneck, generating a meta-improvement mission.

units.name: Meta-Incident
units.text: A distinct incident class beyond "a feature failed": "the institution failed to learn," triggered e.g. when the same bug class appears a fourth time, requiring investigation of CPP itself.

units.name: Compounding Failure Gate
units.text: A mandatory analysis triggered by any repeated failure class asking why the ratchet did not prevent recurrence, preventing "we have memory" from being an unevidenced claim.

units.name: Bidirectional Institutional Evolution
units.text: The principle that a new insight propagates not only forward to future projects but backward, re-examining what historical assumptions it invalidates, what baselines it changes, what benchmarks need updating, and what old projects are exposed.

units.name: Temporal Capability Graph
units.text: A time-indexed version of the capability graph, storing capability state through time to understand how CPP evolved and which improvements produced real inflection points.

units.name: Inflection Point Mining
units.text: A search over historical changes after which TTPE fell, bugs dropped, reuse rose, or autonomy increased, to learn which infrastructure investments produce maximum compounding.

units.name: Meta-Leverage Learning
units.text: A second-order loop where CPP learns which types of improvements tend to produce the greatest compound effect, and adjusts its future allocation accordingly — learning how to improve an engineering institution more effectively, not just learning to code better.

units.name: Institutional Flywheel Controller
units.text: A top-level coordinator (not implementing capabilities itself) that observes the construction stream, capability graph, learning yield, bottlenecks, failures, migrations, benchmarks, frontier, and costs, continuously asking what the highest-leverage next institutional improvement is, distinct from the local per-mission planner's dual optimization (local delivery vs. institutional capacity).
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric

units.name: Dual Optimization
units.text: The rule that every mission operates under two objective functions simultaneously: deliver correctly (local) and increase future capacity (institutional), never sacrificing the real product for abstraction but never ignoring leverage opportunities either.

units.name: Triple and Quadruple Output
units.text: The v2 expansion of mission outputs to four: A-Artifact (what was built), B-Capability Delta (what CPP now does better), C-Learning-System Delta (what CPP learned about how to learn/evaluate/generalize/improve better, the recursive ingredient), and D-Frontier Delta (what higher-level problem became visible/reachable).
entities: Artifact / Capability Delta / Learning-System Delta / Frontier Delta

units.name: Compounding Ladder
units.text: The ascension path a mission's output can climb: Artifact -> Pattern -> Capability -> Primitive -> Platform -> Standard -> Architecture -> Decision Engine -> Autonomous Workflow -> Institutional Infrastructure -> Meta-Capability -> Meta-Architecture -> Improvement Engine, with maximum value when a construction climbs several levels.

units.name: Meta-Capabilities
units.text: Capabilities about improving capabilities (e.g. "debugging" is a capability; "improving debugging systems based on observed failure classes" is a meta-capability; "automatically selecting which debugging improvement has highest downstream leverage" is a layer above that), which CPP should be able to represent explicitly.

units.name: Improvement Infrastructure as First-Class Product
units.text: The rule that improvements to the improvement-engine itself must be treated as an institutional product, not secondary internal tooling, since such an improvement can outvalue many features.
units.canonical_key: improvement infrastructure as first class product

units.name: Recursive Production Reality
units.text: The requirement that even the compounding system itself needs reality verification: "we institutionalized X" is not accepted until a future mission actually used X and got a superior result.

units.name: Institutionalization Is Not Storage
units.text: The constitutional-rank rule that a learning is institutionalized not when stored, but when future behavior changes because of it.

units.name: Compounding Is Not Reuse
units.text: The rule that reuse is only first-order compounding; true compounding requires reuse plus better discovery, evaluation, prioritization, composition, research, and institutionalization.

units.name: Recursive Baseline Law
units.text: The rule that whenever a meta-capability (e.g. root-cause analysis method) improves, it too becomes baseline, and all future incidents — even ones improving other systems — inherit that method.

units.name: Recursive Feedback Topology
units.text: The final loop shape, not a line: Construction <-> Capabilities <-> Evaluators <-> Benchmarks <-> Failures <-> Knowledge <-> Datasets <-> Architecture <-> Tooling <-> Agents <-> Research <-> Governance <-> Meta-Learning <-> Frontier Selection <-> Construction, where any improvement can feed several nodes.

units.name: Typed Causal Feedback Edges
units.text: The constraint that "everything feeds everything" does not mean indiscriminate connection; feedback must only transfer where structural applicability, evidence, causal relevance, and acceptable risk exist — maximum useful feedback, not maximum connection count.

units.name: Compounding Quality Gate
units.text: A gate requiring every new feedback loop to justify that it genuinely increases quality, speed, reliability, learning, or leverage, rather than merely adding complexity.

units.name: Recursive Simplicity
units.text: The design principle that the mature system should feel increasingly automatic, not increasingly heavy: more knowledge and fewer prompts, more evidence and less rediscovery, more guarantees and less policing, more capabilities and less bespoke infrastructure.

units.name: Self-Accelerating Engineering Institution
units.text: The final target state: every construction increases capacity, every capability reduces future cost, every failure increases immunity, every evaluator reveals deeper failures, every benchmark raises mastery, every baseline reduces search space, freeing capacity to attack harder problems that in turn produce capabilities that improve the learning machine itself.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric

units.name: Compounding Conceptual Equation
units.text: A conceptual formula stating future capability equals current capability plus learning times reuse times transfer times composition times learning-system improvement, all of which multipliers can themselves improve over time.

units.name: Sustained Superlinear Compounding Under Reality Constraints
units.text: The caveat that unlimited exponential growth is not assumed; real systems face diminishing returns, irreducible novelty, physical limits, integration costs, changing environments, and uncertainty — the architecture aspires to sustained superlinear compounding where reality permits, and must detect and respond to plateaus.
entities: Sustained Superlinear Compounding Under Reality Constraints
units.canonical_key: sustained superlinear compounding under reality constraints

units.name: UCR-CIF v2 Constitutional Laws
units.text: The v2 set of constitutional laws governing institutional improvement, self-improvement of improvement systems, human corrections as candidate institutional failures, repeated failure as loop-failure evidence, cheaper-on-mastery, leverage evaluation, behavior-changing promotion, periodic challengers, ceremony-cost justification, and frontier escalation.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric

units.name: Recursive Institutional Acceleration
units.text: The named end-state chain where CPP builds better, learns better from what's built, improves its learning systems, selects better improvements, creates better evaluators, discovers deeper failures, produces better abstractions, composes more capabilities, reduces more search space, automates more dominated work, frees more capacity for frontier work, and some resulting capabilities improve the flywheel itself again — an autocatalytic technical institution bounded by evidence, reality, and safety.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric

units.name: Claude Power Pack Recursive Autonomous Engineering & Compounding Execution Protocol
units.text: A constitutional execution protocol adapting the flywheel doctrine into per-session behavior: resolve the immediate need, use maximum real repo context, improve any related layer with clear positive ROI, eliminate root causes not symptoms, avoid reintroducing already-solved problems, convert reusable learning into permanent capability, raise the applicable completion standard, and improve CPP's own planning/execution/validation/learning mechanisms when evidence justifies it; mission ends only with evidence of real, integrated, non-degrading, gap-free, immunity-producing, baseline-raising completion.
entities: Claude Power Pack Recursive Autonomous Engineering & Compounding Execution Protocol
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Compounding Intelligence & Engineering Acceleration Fabric
units.canonical_key: claude power pack recursive autonomous engineering compounding execution protocol

units.name: Kill-Switch Absolute Zero-Code-In-Prompt
units.text: A hard constraint that the execution prompt itself must contain zero code, zero pseudocode, and no prescriptive implementation detail; Claude Code decides implementation, and any instruction pushing toward inventing implementation without inspecting the repo must be overridden by real evidence.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Autonomous Engineering & Compounding Execution Protocol
units.canonical_key: kill switch absolute zero code in prompt

units.name: Reality Principle
units.text: The rule that before assuming architecture, repo structure, components, APIs, contracts, dependencies, paths, state models, tests, persistence, ownership, lifecycle, interfaces, build system, deployment, observability, or tooling, the agent must inspect the real repository; a conversational instruction may describe symptoms or hypotheses but is not authority over facts the repo can demonstrate.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Autonomous Engineering & Compounding Execution Protocol

units.name: Delegation Principle Expanded
units.text: The rule that, except for interpreting conversational intent and compiling the initial mission, every decision whose quality can improve using available execution-time information (repo context, git history, dependencies, call/module graph, runtime, workspace state, tests, CI, logs, metrics, traces, errors, docs, prior architecture decisions, evidence bundles, baselines, knowledge vault, UKDL, CPP systems, session results) is explicitly delegated to Claude Code, which must preserve user intent while freely optimizing means.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Autonomous Engineering & Compounding Execution Protocol

units.name: Opportunity Delegation Principle v2
units.text: The rule that Claude Code must continuously scan for duplication, lower-quality parallel implementations, and debt across technical/architectural/observability/testing/reliability/security/performance/DX/documentation/knowledge dimensions, incorporating high-ROI reasonable-cost improvements automatically while deferring or logging higher-cost/risk ones, gated by an Opportunity ROI Gate scoring expected value, risk reduction, reuse potential, systemic leverage, cost, complexity, blast radius, reversibility, and relation to current work.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Recursive Autonomous Engineering & Compounding Execution Protocol

units.name: Work Mode Router
units.text: A router selecting the minimum sufficient work mode rather than defaulting to ULTRA-PLAN: EXECUTION MODE by default when the problem is well-defined, applicable architecture exists, scope is small/moderate, and decisions can resolve during execution; PLAN MODE when several relevant decisions, non-trivial trade-offs, multiple components, or moderate risk exist.
