units.text: The requirement that IFC itself be examined: given historical states, what would it have prioritized, compared against realized outcomes (backtesting, not to fake historical certainty but to check whether the ranking logic would have caught obvious high-leverage opportunities); a new allocation model may compete against the current IFC (never replaced by intuition); successful allocation patterns move to a regression vault as the frontier rises; and IFC's own competence ascends through basic leverage ranking, causal attribution, portfolio optimization, meta-allocation, and emergent opportunity discovery.
entities: Controller Benchmarks / Allocation Backtesting / Controller Challenger / Controller Regression Vault / IFC Mastering Its Own Job

units.name: Recursive Capital Allocation Loop
units.text: The final closed loop: the engineering system generates opportunities, IFC estimates leverage, selects an investment, engineering improves, the institution produces more evidence, IFC learns its prediction error, the allocation model improves, and the next investment is chosen better.

units.name: Institutional Acceleration Rate
units.text: A central metric asking not just how much CPP improves but whether the rate of improvement is itself rising, required to be reliable/evidence-based/maintainable/complexity-adjusted (not raw growth); distinguishing Nominal Growth (more rules/agents/systems) from Realized Compounding, tested by whether future missions are actually better, faster, less human-dependent, more reliable, and harder-problem-capable — if not, the compounding claim is false.
entities: IAR / Acceleration Quality / Compounding Quality / Realized Compounding Test

units.name: Institutional Productivity Frontier
units.text: A frontier relating human attention + compute + time to Production Excellence, which the institution seeks to push outward; measuring production-grade capability per resource unit (not raw velocity) and tracking conceptual task difficulty so that TTPE reductions from easier tasks don't falsely count as acceleration — the strongest evidence of true acceleration is the institution solving harder problem classes while requiring less marginal effort for already-mastered ones.
entities: Quality-Adjusted Engineering Productivity / Harder-Work Index / True Acceleration Condition

units.name: Institutional Flywheel Health Dashboard
units.text: A conceptual dashboard (Baseline Height, Baseline Coverage, TTPE, OSR, FDR, HIB, Leverage Realization, Capability Reuse, Composition Yield, Search Waste, Decision Surface, Failure Recurrence, Allocation Regret, Learning Velocity, Learning Acceleration, Institutional Complexity) required not to be a vanity dashboard: every metric must be able to change a decision (metric deteriorates -> causal analysis -> candidate improvement -> IFC portfolio); a metric that cannot change action is not part of the control system.
entities: Health-to-Action Compiler / No Dashboard Without Control Loop

units.name: IFC Structured Output Contract
units.text: The required shape of IFC's output, never a bare "Top 10 ideas": Current Binding Constraint, Highest-Leverage Investment, Why (causal path), Expected Downstream Effect, Meta-Leverage, Cost/Risk/Uncertainty, Cheapest Falsification, Promotion Criteria, Kill Criteria, and Next Frontier.

units.name: Capital Allocation State Machine
units.text: An eleven-state lifecycle for every opportunity — Observed, Investigating, Experimenting, Proven, Funded, Implementing, Canary, Promoted, Saturated, Deferred, Rejected — each opportunity carrying a leverage thesis, evidence, consumers, confidence, and lifecycle state (never an opaque ranking); a Saturated capability healthily exits the active investment frontier and can be Reactivated by new evidence.
entities: Opportunity Queue With Explanations / Capital Allocation States

units.name: IFC Time Horizon Balancing
units.text: The requirement that the Controller understand mixed time horizons (short-term return, medium-term infrastructure return, long-term option value) in its portfolio, avoiding both short-termism (not all high ROI appears immediately) and infrastructure romanticism (never build grand platforms on "someday useful" reasoning) — the correct path is local patterns -> repeated patterns -> primitive -> platform, never skipped.
entities: Avoid Short-Termism / Avoid Infrastructure Romanticism / Proof Before Platform

units.name: Opportunity Mining Signals
units.text: A set of named mining signals converting repeated real-world friction into opportunity candidates: repeated workaround -> missing capability candidate; repeated human escalation -> missing autonomy capability; repeated failures -> missing reliability capability; repeated research -> missing knowledge authority; repeated architecture choice -> potential default/decision engine; repeated implementation -> primitive candidate; repeated manual sequence -> workflow/harness candidate; with confidence rising when multiple signal types converge on the same gap.
entities: Demand-Side Signal / Latent Demand / Workaround Mining / Escalation Mining / Incident Mining / Search Mining / Decision Mining / Code Duplication Mining / Manual Process Mining / Multi-Signal Opportunity Confidence

units.name: IFC Causal Graph Learning
units.text: The evolution of IFC from correlation ranking to causal understanding: opportunities backed by multiple independent evidence types get special attention; improving X and observing whether the expected downstream change actually occurs (and updating the graph if not) treats every engineering change as an experiment on the causal graph, revising dependency assumptions when predicted propagation fails.
entities: Cross-System Evidence Fusion / Institutional Causal Discovery / Causal Intervention / Graph Learns From Interventions / Structural Model Revision

units.name: Institutional Engineering Digital Twin
units.text: A long-term approximation IFC develops — not a full replica but a model sufficient to predict where an investment will help — used to simulate likely effects before high-cost changes as an aid to experiment design (never as truth), with production results always overriding simulated predictions, and prediction errors updating the twin's edges, priors, and leverage estimates.
entities: Simulation Before Expensive Action / Reality Always Wins / Self-Correcting Digital Twin

units.name: Controller Failure as Institutional Incident
units.text: The rule that IFC repeatedly misallocating capital is itself an Allocation System Incident requiring root-causing (classes include overestimated reuse, underestimated integration cost, ignored bottleneck, poor causal graph, weak uncertainty calibration, over-optimization of a short-term metric), with the Controller's own mistakes ascending to allocation hard rules, process rules, or traps in IFC's own UKDL.

units.name: Traceable Leverage Scoring
units.text: The rule that any IFC leverage score must be explainable by its supporting evidence and causal paths — opaque scores create false authority; every ranking must be accompanied by rationale, never presented as ground truth.
entities: No Global Number Without Traceability / Score as Decision Support Not Truth

units.name: IFC Human Governance Interface
units.text: The rule that major institutional reallocations may still require Owner approval, but IFC must have already done all the technical cognition, presenting decision, evidence, trade-offs, and recommendation (never an incomplete investigation); the Owner ideally focuses on strategic goals, risk appetite, and value judgments (e.g. "prioritize reliability and autonomy") which IFC compiles into a concrete leverage portfolio, with objective weights changing as strategy changes while safety/correctness floors remain constitutionally stable.
entities: Human Governance (IFC) / Owner Capital Allocation Role / Strategy to Engineering Allocation Compiler / Dynamic Objective Weights / Constitutional Constraints Are Stable

units.name: Institutional Flywheel Controller Constitution
units.text: The ten constitutional laws of IFC: evaluate effort by expected marginal institutional return when positive-ROI to do so; direct feature value must not obscure transitive/compositional/meta-leverage; target the strongest binding constraint, not the loudest symptom; a capability's value includes all downstream consumers; evaluation/learning/context/research/debugging/allocation improvements get explicit meta-leverage weight; marginal return (not historical importance) drives capital flow; new evidence must be allowed to invalidate old priorities; high-uncertainty high-impact investments buy information before irreversible commitment; compounding is measured by future behavioral improvement, not artifact count; the Controller itself must learn from expected-vs-realized leverage gaps.

units.name: IFC Master Loop
units.text: The full IFC cycle: observe entire institution -> build current state graph -> identify bottlenecks -> discover improvement opportunities -> estimate direct+transitive+compositional+meta+autonomy leverage+option value -> adjust for cost+risk+uncertainty+complexity -> identify cheapest falsification -> experiment -> observe real effect -> update causal graph -> promote/reject/iterate -> recompute bottleneck -> select next investment -> repeat.

units.name: IFC Recursive Loop
units.text: The loop above the master loop: IFC predicts the best investment, investment happens, realized leverage is measured, prediction error is calculated, the allocation model improves, future investment selection improves, higher-value improvements happen sooner, the institution accelerates faster, more evidence becomes available, and IFC improves again — the flywheel learns where to push itself.

units.name: UCR-CIF plus HIC-OAR plus IFC Convergence
units.text: The unification of the three systems: UCR-CIF converts every construction into institutional capital, HIC-OAR converts every avoidable human intervention into an autonomy capability, and IFC decides which of all these opportunities deserves engineering first — forming the pipeline construction produces evidence -> UCR-CIF extracts capabilities -> HIC-OAR extracts human-dependency gaps -> failure systems extract immunity gaps -> knowledge systems extract knowledge gaps -> IFC observes all gaps together -> selects highest-leverage improvement -> strengthens multiple systems -> future constructions improve -> future interventions fall -> more advanced failures become visible -> new opportunities appear -> IFC reallocates.
entities: UCR-CIF plus HIC-OAR plus IFC Convergence
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Institutional Flywheel Controller
units.canonical_key: ucr cif plus hic oar plus ifc convergence

units.name: Institutional Improvement Strategy Intelligence
units.text: A superior IFC state beyond selecting known best improvements: detecting improvements nobody has proposed, predicting which could create new capability families, designing cheap experiments to validate them, discovering positive feedback loops, reallocating effort toward them, measuring realized compound effect, and improving its own capital-allocation model — CPP begins learning which types of engineering investments most reliably improve the whole institution.
units.parent: UCR-CIF plus HIC-OAR plus IFC Convergence

units.name: IFC North Star
units.text: The proposed IFC North Star, replacing a bare Leverage Score: Compounding-Adjusted Time to Production Excellence, observed jointly with Task Difficulty, Production Reality Correctness, One-Shot Rate, Capability Coverage, and Reusable Intelligence all rising while Human Intervention, Search Waste, Decision Surface, False Done, Failure Recurrence, Engineering Effort per Mastered Problem Class, and Institutional Complexity per Unit Capability all fall.

units.name: IFC Final Law
units.text: The closing IFC law: do not merely make Claude Power Pack better; learn which improvements make it better fastest; then improve the system that identifies those improvements; then use that resulting capability to choose even higher-leverage improvements; repeat under reality, evidence, risk, simplicity, and production-quality constraints — turning CPP's technical growth from accumulation of improvements into recursively improving engineering capital allocation.

units.name: Claude Power Pack Universal Failure Immunity, Anticipation & Error-Derived Baseline Flywheel
units.text: A system extending UCR-CIF, HIC-OAR, IFC, UKDL, Knowledge Vault, Production Reality Gate, Completion Standard Ratchet, and Kernel vMAX-NULL-ERROR, whose mission is that every failure increases the probability that an entire future failure family is prevented before occurrence, or failing that, makes that family cheaper, earlier, and more deterministic to detect and resolve — the institutional cost of repeating a known failure class must approach zero, and every new failure must expand CPP's predictive failure envelope.
entities: Claude Power Pack Universal Failure Immunity, Anticipation & Error-Derived Baseline Flywheel
units.canonical_key: claude power pack universal failure immunity anticipation error derived baseline flywheel

units.name: Failure Mechanism as Fundamental Unit
units.text: The rule that an individual bug is only a manifestation; the important institutional unit is the failure mechanism — e.g. "button doesn't work" is a symptom of "UI control -> no registered command -> no backend route -> fake visual completion," generalized as "user-reachable control must have a verified causal path to its claimed effect," protecting buttons, menu items, CLI commands, RPC calls, background actions, webhooks, and automations alike.
units.parent: Claude Power Pack Universal Failure Immunity, Anticipation & Error-Derived Baseline Flywheel

units.name: Session Failure Stream
units.text: A comprehensive capture stream for every relevant failure occurring anywhere in a session — not just user-reported bugs but failing/flaky tests, build errors, runtime exceptions, integration/CLI/frontend/backend/persistence failures, race conditions, dependency/configuration/packaging/deployment failures, environment incompatibilities, corrupted data, retry/recovery failures, observability blind spots, false-positive tests, false Done, manual intervention, architecture contradictions, documentation/runtime divergence, performance cliffs, security failures, tooling/agent/orchestration failures — an incidentally-discovered error remains valid evidence.

units.name: Failure Distillation Pipeline
units.text: A pipeline preventing raw failure noise from contaminating the institution: Raw Failure Event -> Material Failure -> Failure Class -> Institutional Failure Knowledge -> Universal Failure Knowledge -> Baseline Immunity, with a separate triage classifying scope as Incidental, Local, Recurring, Archetype, Stack, Cross-Stack, Universal, or Constitutional — not everything ascends, but every material failure receives a classification.
entities: Error Telemetry vs Error Knowledge / Failure Triage Gate

units.name: Universal Failure Record
units.text: The required structured record for every institutionally relevant failure: observable symptom, affected artifact, context, environment, trigger, expected/actual behavior, reproduction evidence, causal chain, root cause, violated invariant, detection gap, why tests/architecture missed it, blast radius, related failure classes, remediation, regression, prevention opportunities, applicability, confidence, source commits, Production Reality evidence, and transfer candidates — causal structure, not narrative prose.

units.name: Knowledge Vault and UKDL Functional Split
units.text: The critical distinction that the Knowledge Vault holds long-form evidence memory (context, incidents, experiments, causal analysis, regressions, counterexamples, alternative hypotheses, historical evolution) while UKDL holds compressed, operational, executable doctrine across Hard Rules/Process Rules/Traps, each entry additionally declaring trigger conditions, applicability, rationale pointer, severity, confidence, detector, prevention surface, relevant failure family, and supersession state — turning UKDL from a "best practices manual" into failure-derived execution priors.
entities: Knowledge Vault and UKDL Functional Split
KNOWLEDGE VAULT = LONG-FORM EVIDENCE MEMORY / UKDL = COMPRESSED EXECUTABLE DOCTRINE
units.canonical_key: knowledge vault and ukdl functional split

units.name: UKDL Must Change Execution
units.text: The rule that a UKDL entry is not institutionalized merely by existing — it must change planning, implementation, verification, test selection, architectural review, or Production Reality gates; knowledge without a future execution consumer is incomplete institutionalization.
units.parent: Knowledge Vault and UKDL Functional Split

units.name: Failure Distillation Ladder
units.text: The ten-rung ladder every material failure should climb: L0 Fact, L1 Reproducer, L2 Root Cause, L3 Violated Invariant, L4 Failure Family, L5 Generalization, L6 Detector, L7 Preventer, L8 Baseline, L9 Predictive Model (what conditions announce rising risk).

units.name: Bug Fix Is Not Failure Closure
units.text: The rule that a fixed line does not close the institutional incident; closure requires answering what caused it, what family it represents, what other places are exposed, how recurrence is detected and prevented, what future work will learn, what baseline must change, and how we'll know the learning is actually used.
entities: Bug Fix Is Not Failure Closure
units.canonical_key: bug fix is not failure closure

units.name: Failure Genome
units.text: A structured causal record per failure family: preconditions, trigger, hidden assumption, broken invariant, propagation, observability, escape mechanism (why gates missed it), detection opportunity, prevention opportunity, and recovery — enabling transfer between apparently unrelated software.
units.parent: Bug Fix Is Not Failure Closure

units.name: Causal Abstraction (Failure Genome Example)
units.text: An illustration of proper generalization: a Git ENOENT caused by inherited PATH differences should not distill to "look for Git in Program Files" but to "external tool discovery must not assume interactive-shell environment equivalence," protecting Git, Python, Java, FFmpeg, Docker, compilers, package managers, and other external CLIs at once.

units.name: Generalization Search and Exposure Graph
units.text: After root cause, asking where else the same causal mechanism can exist (same abstraction, boundary, lifecycle, state model, trust assumption, or integration topology, not just identical text), building a Failure Exposure Graph (nodes: modules/interfaces/subsystems/projects/primitives/workflows; edges: shares causal exposure) and proactively scanning it for other exposed locations before closing an incident — proactive bug hunting derived from real evidence.

units.name: Latent Failure Discovery
units.text: A subsystem taking a Failure Genome as input and, by asking which systems share the same preconditions, trigger variants, amplifying lifecycle states, or cross-component compositions, producing evidence-based failure hypotheses for latent (not-yet-occurred) failures — a single production bug can eliminate several future incidents before their first manifestation.

units.name: Predictive Failure Pack
units.text: A pack the Baseline Compiler generates before any new mission, based on language, runtime, architecture, touched modules, statefulness, concurrency, external tools, persistence, integrations, network, UI, lifecycle, and historical failure genomes, telling the planner which failure families are especially plausible here — consulted before modifying a stateful subsystem (state-loss, partial-write, stale-state, restart, rollback genomes) so historical failures actively shape future planning.

units.name: Diff-Aware Failure Prediction
units.text: A dynamic update to the Predictive Failure Pack during execution: if the diff introduces a subprocess, async boundary, persistence, cache, retry, external command, or mutable global state, new relevant failure families activate; the current diff plus architecture plus failure genomes compiles into a change-specific risk model guiding test and adversarial-scenario selection.

units.name: Test Selection from Failure Memory
units.text: The rule that verification should not always run an identical suite; known relevant failure families should select regression, integration, property, adversarial, and lifecycle tests — failure memory guides verification.

units.name: Failure-Derived Adversarial Generation
units.text: Generation of variant adversarial cases from each Failure Genome (e.g. dependency missing -> wrong version, spaced path, permission denied, environment changed post-startup, dependency disappearing mid-session), plus counterfactual mining (what small change would have made this failure worse/harder-to-detect/more-expensive) and neighborhood testing around the failure boundary rather than only the exact reproducer, reducing regression overfitting.

units.name: Compositional Failure Synthesis
units.text: Deliberate combination of Failure Genomes (e.g. partial persistence + process crash + retry -> duplicate execution) to anticipate a fourth failure from three separate learnings, prioritizing causally-compatible, high-severity, architecture-relevant combinations (not indiscriminate combinatorial explosion) — failure classes, like capabilities, can emerge from composition (e.g. state caching + hot reload + external mutation -> stale-reality failures) and can be derived without anyone experiencing them first.
entities: Failure Recombination / Failure Combination Miner / Emergent Failure Detection

units.name: Pre-Incident Immunity
units.text: The fundamental leap from failure->immunity to failure A -> generalized causal knowledge -> predicts failure B -> B prevented -> no incident required — the institution begins learning beyond the bugs it has actually experienced.

units.name: Bug-to-Invariant Compiler
units.text: The requirement that every important failure attempt to produce a reusable invariant (e.g. a backup published before fsync becomes "durability claims require stable storage before publication") — the invariant is far more reusable than the specific fix.

units.name: Invariant-to-Enforcement Ascension
units.text: The maturation path of an invariant from prose rule to test to validator to static check to runtime guard to primitive when technically applicable — mature knowledge is not "remember to do it" but making the wrong thing difficult or impossible.

units.name: Defense-in-Depth Ascension
units.text: The rule that a high-severity failure family should not depend on a single protection layer (prevention, early detection, runtime guard, recovery, regression, so losing one layer doesn't destroy immunity), while also favoring the cheapest structural prevention layer (API design, type system, static validator, test, build gate, over runtime assertion) rather than converting everything into recurring runtime overhead.

units.name: CACHE LIFECYCLE GENOME
units.text: Relational failure pattern where a resource still semantically active has its inactivity timer expire, causing cache unload, and a downstream consumer reads unavailable state.

units.name: REPRESENTATION DIVERGENCE GENOME
units.text: Relational failure where an in-memory mutation succeeds but a derived field is not updated, so durable serialization persists a stale value revealed on restart.

units.name: STALE REPLICA DESTRUCTIVE MUTATION GENOME
units.text: Relational failure where a node with a stale local snapshot treats absence as authoritative and emits a deletion, losing newer remote state.

units.name: CRITICAL-THREAD I/O GENOME
units.text: Relational failure where a compatibility-API request causes a cache miss requiring durable lookup while the caller runs on a latency-critical thread, producing a correctness/performance conflict.

units.name: EVERY REPEATED HUMAN DEBUGGING QUESTION SHOULD BECOME AN INTROSPECTION CAPABILITY
units.text: A CPP law stating a recurring human debugging question must be converted into a machine-queryable introspection capability (e.g. Agent Decision Trace, Cache Provenance Inspector, Effect Causal Trace, Mutation History, UBC Decision Trace).
entities: EVERY REPEATED HUMAN DEBUGGING QUESTION SHOULD BECOME AN INTROSPECTION CAPABILITY
units.canonical_key: every repeated human debugging question should become an introspection capability

units.name: QueryOptions for baseline compilation
units.text: A LuckPerms-inspired concept where baseline capsule selection depends on a structured context (Mission Type, Runtime, Risk, Statefulness, Distribution, Persistence, Public API, Security, Lifecycle, Environment) analogous to permission QueryOptions.

units.name: BASELINE CAPSULES BECOME CONTEXT-INDEXED ENGINEERING DECISIONS
units.text: There is no absolute global best practice; only the best applicable verified baseline under given Query Options.
entities: BASELINE CAPSULES BECOME CONTEXT-INDEXED ENGINEERING DECISIONS
units.canonical_key: baseline capsules become context indexed engineering decisions

units.name: INHERITED STATE CORRECTNESS RATIO
units.text: Measures how much of the hard problem of authority, cache, freshness, contexts, lifecycle, synchronization, concurrency is already solved by institutional infrastructure before local novelty is implemented.

units.name: Contextual Correctness Escape Rate
units.text: Counts bugs that survive because a function worked in the normal case but failed under another context, offline state, stale cache, other runtime, reconnection, migration, or multi-node race. Target: decreasing.

units.name: State Divergence Detection Latency
units.text: Time elapsed between two representations losing agreement and CPP detecting it. Target near zero for critical state.

units.name: Authority Ambiguity Rate
units.text: Counts how often the system cannot determine which representation holds the truth for a given datum in a lifecycle phase. Target zero.

units.name: Decision Explainability Coverage
units.text: Percentage of critical decisions (policies/agents/routing) that can answer "why did this happen" with machine-readable evidence. Target ~100%.

units.name: NO STATEFUL SYSTEM MAY HAVE MULTIPLE REPRESENTATIONS OF THE SAME FACT WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT AUTHORITY, SYNCHRONIZATION AND DIVERGENCE-DETECTION CONTRACT
units.text: Constitutional law requiring explicit authority/sync/divergence-detection contracts for any multi-representation state.
entities: NO STATEFUL SYSTEM MAY HAVE MULTIPLE REPRESENTATIONS OF THE SAME FACT WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT AUTHORITY, SYNCHRONIZATION AND DIVERGENCE-DETECTION CONTRACT
units.canonical_key: no stateful system may have multiple representations of the same fact without an explicit authority synchronization and divergence detection contract

units.name: NO CACHE MAY EXIST WITHOUT A DECLARED FRESHNESS, INVALIDATION AND LIFECYCLE MODEL PROPORTIONAL TO ITS CONSEQUENCE
units.text: Constitutional law requiring every cache to declare a freshness/invalidation/lifecycle model sized to its consequence.
entities: NO CACHE MAY EXIST WITHOUT A DECLARED FRESHNESS, INVALIDATION AND LIFECYCLE MODEL PROPORTIONAL TO ITS CONSEQUENCE
units.canonical_key: no cache may exist without a declared freshness invalidation and lifecycle model proportional to its consequence

units.name: NO POLICY OR CONTEXT-DEPENDENT DECISION MAY BE CONSIDERED MATURE IF ITS RESULT CANNOT BE EXPLAINED FROM ITS INPUT CONTEXT AND CONTRIBUTING RULES
units.text: Constitutional law tying maturity of a policy/context decision to explainability of its result.
entities: NO POLICY OR CONTEXT-DEPENDENT DECISION MAY BE CONSIDERED MATURE IF ITS RESULT CANNOT BE EXPLAINED FROM ITS INPUT CONTEXT AND CONTRIBUTING RULES
units.canonical_key: no policy or context dependent decision may be considered mature if its result cannot be explained from its input context and contributing rules

units.name: NO LATENCY-UNBOUNDED OPERATION MAY SILENTLY ENTER A LATENCY-CRITICAL EXECUTION PATH
units.text: Constitutional law forbidding unbounded-latency operations from silently entering latency-critical paths.
entities: NO LATENCY-UNBOUNDED OPERATION MAY SILENTLY ENTER A LATENCY-CRITICAL EXECUTION PATH
units.canonical_key: no latency unbounded operation may silently enter a latency critical execution path

units.name: SHARED STORAGE DOES NOT IMPLY SHARED REALITY
units.text: Constitutional law: propagation, invalidation and reconciliation must be explicit even when storage is shared.
entities: SHARED STORAGE DOES NOT IMPLY SHARED REALITY
units.canonical_key: shared storage does not imply shared reality

units.name: A VALUE WITHOUT ITS AUTHORITY, FRESHNESS AND CONTEXT IS NOT COMPLETE STATE
units.text: The deepest of the LuckPerms-derived laws: a value is not complete state unless paired with its authority, freshness, and context.
entities: A VALUE WITHOUT ITS AUTHORITY, FRESHNESS AND CONTEXT IS NOT COMPLETE STATE
units.canonical_key: a value without its authority freshness and context is not complete state

units.name: LuckPerms Longitudinal State & Policy Maturity Corpus
units.text: A dedicated branch of Historical Software Maturity Distillation that ingests LuckPerms' 2,269 commits, tags v4.x-v5.5, issues, PRs, wiki history, API evolution, storage migrations, platform adaptations and bug reports through the causal-reconstruction pipeline.
entities: LuckPerms Longitudinal State & Policy Maturity Corpus
units.canonical_key: luckperms longitudinal state policy maturity corpus

units.name: DO NOT COPY LUCKPERMS ARCHITECTURE INTO UNRELATED SOFTWARE
units.text: Hard rule that CPP must distill the causal pressures that forced LuckPerms to mature rather than copy its architecture wholesale, applying only the portion relevant to the current system.
entities: DO NOT COPY LUCKPERMS ARCHITECTURE INTO UNRELATED SOFTWARE
units.parent: LuckPerms Longitudinal State & Policy Maturity Corpus
units.canonical_key: do not copy luckperms architecture into unrelated software

units.name: Constitutive Baseline Ratchet
units.text: Law that a new capability which becomes part of what it means to correctly build a class of system stops being an optional feature and becomes constitutive baseline inherited by future equivalent constructions.

units.name: Constitutive Promotion Gate
units.text: A 4-question gate (incidental? product-specific? archetype-enhancing? constitutive?) that decides whether a new feature is promoted into a family's constitutive baseline; only archetype-enhancing/constitutive features qualify.

units.name: Instance Baseline / System-Family Baseline / Architecture-Archetype Baseline / Domain Baseline / Universal Production Baseline
units.text: Five-tier baseline hierarchy the UBC manages, from what a single instance must preserve up to what applies transversally to all software.
entities: Instance Baseline / System-Family Baseline / Architecture-Archetype Baseline / Domain Baseline / Universal Production Baseline
units.canonical_key: instance baseline system family baseline architecture archetype baseline domain baseline universal production baseline

units.name: Constitutive Capability Set
units.text: Per-system registry answering "what capabilities are now inseparable from this thing's correct construction" — not files present, not features ever received.

units.name: Constitutive Baseline Regression
units.text: Detector that fires when a new instance of a family omits a capability already constitutive to that family without an applicability exception — classified as more severe than a missing nice-to-have.

units.name: NO FEATURE REDISCOVERY
units.text: Law that once a feature is elevated to constitutive baseline, the user must never have to re-request it; if it happens, it is logged as a UBC retrieval/applicability/compilation/authority failure institutional incident.

units.name: Baseline Propagation Set
units.text: Classification (IMMEDIATE / RATCHET-ON-TOUCH / OPTIONAL MIGRATION) of which existing instances below a newly raised baseline should receive backpropagated upgrades and when.

units.name: Feature maturity state ladder
units.text: Ladder a feature ascends through: LOCAL_EXPERIMENT -> LOCAL_VERIFIED -> INSTANCE_STANDARD -> FAMILY_CANDIDATE -> FAMILY_BASELINE -> CROSS_ARCHETYPE -> DOMAIN_BASELINE -> UNIVERSAL_CANDIDATE -> UNIVERSAL_BASELINE.

units.name: COMPLETENESS IS HERITABLE
units.text: Law that once a system type (e.g. Agent Runtime) reaches a completeness level (resumability, observability, context recovery, tool error recovery, deterministic state, cancellation, provenance), the next build of that type starts with those as starting conditions, not backlog.

units.name: Feature to Done-Gate propagation
units.text: Rule that when a capability becomes constitutive, the corresponding Done-Gate definition changes so omitting it blocks completion even if unspecified in the prompt.

units.name: Certified Atomic Persistence Primitive
units.text: Example of a feature-to-primitive trajectory: atomic persistence stops being reimplemented per project and becomes a default certified infrastructure primitive referenced by baseline.

units.name: Capability Composition Contracts
units.text: Baseline extension stating that when capability A and capability B co-occur (e.g. retries+side effects, cache+distributed mutation), capability C (idempotency, reconciliation) becomes newly necessary.

units.name: Baseline emergent requirement discovery
units.text: UBC's ability to detect a requirement (e.g. replay-safe task execution) emergent from a composition of features (background workers + restart recovery + durable queue) without it being explicitly requested.

units.name: Architecture Baseline evolution trigger
units.text: Rule that if a recurring feature always requires hacking existing architecture, that signals a poor architecture baseline; the fix propagates from feature-level lesson to architecture-baseline change (e.g. shared runtime for plugins).

units.name: System Family Identity
units.text: Named identity classes (e.g. STATEFUL_DESKTOP_TERMINAL, AUTONOMOUS_AGENT_RUNTIME, SAFE_WORLD_RETROFIT_ENGINE, PLUGIN_PLATFORM, RESEARCH_PIPELINE) each paired with a Current Constitutive Baseline for UBC recognition.

units.name: Baseline generation per family
units.text: Per-family versioned baseline generations (e.g. AgentRuntime-B17, PluginSystem-B9, StatefulDesktop-B23, DataMigration-B11, SafeMutation-B14) composed by UBC per mission.

units.name: Feature Capitalization Ratio
units.text: Of all features with reuse potential, the percentage that actually became institutional capability/baseline; guards against excellent software with a poor flywheel because gains stay locked in one project.

units.name: Baseline Inheritance Rate
units.text: Percentage of a new instance's applicable constitutive baseline that was inherited automatically when built. Target near 100%.

units.name: Rediscovered Feature Rate
units.text: Counts how often a user had to re-request a capability already constitutive in an equivalent system. Target zero.

units.name: Completeness Regression Rate
units.text: Counts how many new constructions start below the best-verified completeness already demonstrated for their class. Target zero; flagged as especially important for CPP.

units.name: THE BEST VERIFIED COMPLETE IMPLEMENTATION OF A SYSTEM FAMILY DEFINES THE MINIMUM STARTING MATURITY FOR FUTURE APPLICABLE IMPLEMENTATIONS OF THAT FAMILY
units.text: Strongest law of the ratchet section: the best verified implementation sets the floor maturity for future builds of the same family (inheriting demonstrated maturity, not copying the system).
entities: THE BEST VERIFIED COMPLETE IMPLEMENTATION OF A SYSTEM FAMILY DEFINES THE MINIMUM STARTING MATURITY FOR FUTURE APPLICABLE IMPLEMENTATIONS OF THAT FAMILY
units.canonical_key: the best verified complete implementation of a system family defines the minimum starting maturity for future applicable implementations of that family

units.name: WHEN A NEW FEATURE PERMANENTLY CHANGES WHAT WE CONSIDER A COMPLETE INSTANCE OF A SYSTEM FAMILY, THAT FEATURE MUST BE PROMOTED FROM PRODUCT FEATURE TO CONSTITUTIVE BASELINE CAPABILITY
units.text: Precise restatement of the constitutive-promotion law tying permanent completeness redefinition to mandatory baseline promotion.
entities: WHEN A NEW FEATURE PERMANENTLY CHANGES WHAT WE CONSIDER A COMPLETE INSTANCE OF A SYSTEM FAMILY, THAT FEATURE MUST BE PROMOTED FROM PRODUCT FEATURE TO CONSTITUTIVE BASELINE CAPABILITY
units.canonical_key: when a new feature permanently changes what we consider a complete instance of a system family that feature must be promoted from product feature to constitutive baseline capability

units.name: NO FUTURE SYSTEM MAY SILENTLY START BELOW THE BEST VERIFIED APPLICABLE COMPLETENESS BASELINE ALREADY ACHIEVED BY ITS SYSTEM FAMILY
units.text: Explicit constitutional law of Claude Power Pack closing the constitutive ratchet loop: work accumulates heritable maturity, not just code.
entities: NO FUTURE SYSTEM MAY SILENTLY START BELOW THE BEST VERIFIED APPLICABLE COMPLETENESS BASELINE ALREADY ACHIEVED BY ITS SYSTEM FAMILY
units.canonical_key: no future system may silently start below the best verified applicable completeness baseline already achieved by its system family

units.name: Universal Software Integrity & Foresight Baseline
units.text: A universalized version of KIFS (originally Minecraft-domain) that adds the capacity to ask what could still be wrong, incomplete, out of place, unjustified, accidentally correct, or dangerously uncertain even when execution looks correct; compiled dynamically by the UBC alongside maturity baselines.

units.name: System Legitimacy questioning (WHY DOES THIS THING HAVE THE RIGHT TO EXIST)
units.text: Extension of correctness checks beyond "does it work" to "should it exist here, who owns it, what would happen if it disappeared" — universalizing KIFS's setup-legitimacy questions to any artifact.
entities: System Legitimacy questioning (WHY DOES THIS THING HAVE THE RIGHT TO EXIST)
units.canonical_key: system legitimacy questioning why does this thing have the right to exist

units.name: Universal Provenance & Lineage Intelligence
units.text: Generalization of KIFS setup-lineage tracking to any artifact (files, modules, services, schemas, APIs, agents, datasets, prompts, infrastructure, deployment artifacts) via relations like created-by, generated-by, copied-from, forked-from, migrated-from, restored-from, inherited-from, supersedes/superseded-by, packaged-from, deployed-from, hotfixed-from.

units.name: Inherited Artifacts Do Not Inherit Legitimacy
units.text: Universal law that a component from a template, starter repo, fork, previous product, migration, shared library, or backup does not automatically earn the right to remain — it must stay compatible with current intent, ownership, capability requirements, architecture, lifecycle.
entities: Inherited Artifacts Do Not Inherit Legitimacy
units.canonical_key: inherited artifacts do not inherit legitimacy

units.name: Universal Ownership Graph
units.text: Multi-dimensional ownership model (functional, state, decision, lifecycle, experience, operational ownership) generalized from KIFS's player-visible-state ownership findings.

units.name: Capability Legitimacy & Semantic Duplication check
units.text: UBC+USIFB gate that, before introducing a new logger/cache/queue/state-manager/etc, asks what capability is needed, who is the current provider, and why another provider is justified — comparing capabilities not package names, killing semantic duplication.

units.name: CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION + WRONG BOUNDARY = DEFECT
units.text: Law that a capability can be implemented correctly yet be defective because it lives in the wrong service/layer/scope (frontend vs backend, feature vs shared runtime, production vs debug, global vs tenant-local).

units.name: Lifecycle Intelligence universal (state machine)
units.text: Universal artifact lifecycle states (ACTIVE, EXPERIMENTAL, MIGRATION_ONLY, TEMPORARY, DEPRECATED, SUPERSEDED, QUARANTINED, ARCHIVED, BACKUP_ONLY, DEBUG_ONLY, REMOVED) with governed/forbidden transitions (e.g. BACKUP_ONLY->PRODUCTION must be blocked).

units.name: Historical Sediment Hunter
units.text: Searches for artifacts that were once legitimate but may no longer be (unconsumed compatibility shims, retired feature flags, completed migrations, old APIs, stale permissions/config/metrics/tests, dead deployment scripts, fallbacks whose original problem vanished) — distinct from ordinary dead-code analysis since sediment can still execute.

units.name: Negative Necessity Testing
units.text: Conceptually models removal of an artifact (library, service, config, agent, database, workflow, feature flag, compatibility layer) without deleting it; if no observable capability disappears, suspicion rises.

units.name: Reconstruction Test
units.text: For long-lived software, asks what parts of the historical system would not be rebuilt if reconstructed today from current requirements; the delta between historical state and clean reconstruction reveals legacy, accidental coupling, duplicated architecture, dead compatibility.

units.name: Intent-to-Reality Diff universal
units.text: Generalizes KIFS's multi-state comparison into Intended State, Source State, Built State, Deployed State, Runtime State, User Reality, Historical Residue; divergence between any pair is a finding.

units.name: Source -> Build -> Deploy -> Runtime Consistency
units.text: Mandatory-where-applicable check preventing installing old builds, modifying generated output, running mismatched config, deploying a build not matching the commit, or correct binary with incorrect config — strengthens Production Reality.

units.name: Autonomous Integrity Hunter
units.text: A suite of specialized hunters (Invariant Hunter, Semantic Duplicate Hunter, Contamination Hunter, Dead/Orphan Hunter, Consistency Hunter, Experience Hunter, Adversarial Reviewer, Repo-Wide Anomaly Detector) generalized from the KIFS corpus.

units.name: UNKNOWN-UNKNOWN DISCOVERY
units.text: USIFB capability that asks not only "does this violate a known rule" but "what can't I explain, what's surprising, what seems needlessly complex, what's uniquely different without reason, what's suspiciously identical, what depends too much on history, what part of the system nobody observes."

units.name: Structural Anomaly Detection
units.text: Learns normal topology but never conflates normal with correct, since a template-propagated error can become the statistical majority; combines statistical anomaly with semantic legitimacy checking.

units.name: Suspicious Similarity Detection
units.text: Looks for what is suspiciously identical across services/repos/agents (same unneeded dependency, same config, same workaround) as evidence of template contamination.

units.name: Fresh-Eyes Review
units.text: A reviewer deliberately unconditioned by history/taxonomy/existing justifications, asked to explain why things exist, then validated by a contextual reviewer — a countermeasure to normalization blindness.

units.name: Independent Adversarial Review
units.text: Separates executor and auditor and prevents the reviewer from seeing the executor's conclusion first, avoiding anchoring; flags that Agent Teams can be nominally diverse but not epistemologically diverse if given the same framing/evidence.
entities: REVIEW INDEPENDENCE IS AN ENGINEERING PROPERTY

units.name: Blind-Spot Discovery
units.text: High-leverage capability that searches not for bugs but for what is not being observed at all — unaudited modules, untested endpoints, unowned state, schemaless config, unprobed failure paths, deployments without rollback tests, unchecked user output, log-only-known production behavior.

units.name: Hypothesis Generation (USIFB)
units.text: Generates falsifiable hypotheses (hidden second writer? cache outliving its source? mixed rollout producing different semantics? fallback hiding failure?) then applies cheap falsification, converting QA into investigation.

units.name: Metamorphic Testing
units.text: Tests that altering something declared independent (element order, backup removal, display-string rename, unrelated tenant change) should not affect output; a change indicates hidden coupling.

units.name: Counterfactual Auditing
units.text: Asks what would happen without this piece, with a second instance, after restart, if the provider fails, if the user doesn't follow the happy path — used to find Validity-by-Accident.

units.name: Validity-by-Accident Detector
units.text: Supercapability asking whether something is correct by construction or only correct because current circumstances haven't yet challenged it (e.g. single provider, no restart yet, no scaling yet) — true foresight.

units.name: Latent Contradiction Detector
units.text: Detects that two currently-valid facts A and B will fail together once a future condition C appears (e.g. a BACKUP_ONLY artifact matched by a packaging wildcard, waiting for a matching file) — prevention before an incident exists.

units.name: Forbidden-State Search
units.text: Declares states that must never exist (backup executable in production, exposed debug endpoint, deprecated provider receiving writes, two canonical owners, UNKNOWN interpreted as PASS, cancelled job later committing effect, manually-edited generated artifact) and searches for them proactively.

units.name: Forbidden-Transition Search
units.text: Complements Forbidden-State Search by declaring forbidden state-machine transitions (ARCHIVED->ACTIVE without restore, FAILED->DONE without new evidence, TEST->PRODUCTION accidentally, GENERATED->AUTHORITATIVE, PURGED->PACKAGED), making state-machine integrity a baseline property.

units.name: Dependency-on-Circumstance Search
units.text: Asks what environmental assumptions make a correct-looking state possible (single instance, single writer, current load order, current OS, current dependency version, current low traffic), producing explicit assumptions.

units.name: Explainability Scanner
units.text: For each important entity, checks whether it can answer why it exists, who owns it, who consumes it, source authority, lifecycle, current status; inability doesn't prove a bug but is an epistemic integrity finding.

units.name: Epistemic Integrity
units.text: Adds an UNKNOWN category (alongside CORRECT/INCORRECT) for state that cannot be established as correct or incorrect — never a blocker automatically but never a PASS either; aligns with the CORRECT/INCORRECT/UNKNOWN + VERIFIED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/HYPOTHESIS/CONFLICTING evidence taxonomy.

units.name: Scope-Limited Certainty
units.text: Hard rule that any auditor must record searched scope, excluded scope, confidence, and recall limitations; absence of a finding in the searched scope is not proof of non-existence.
entities: NOT FOUND IN SEARCHED SCOPE != DOES NOT EXIST

units.name: Search Recall Integrity
units.text: A search can "succeed" (return without error) and still be incomplete; successful search is not equivalent to exhaustive inventory, applicable to grep/indexes/registries/dependency scans/semantic search.

units.name: Evidence Independence
units.text: Five agents viewing the same information, or five tests from the same faulty oracle, are not independent confirmations; USIFB must model true independence to avoid false confidence.

units.name: Circular Authority Detection
units.text: Detects self-referential verification (expected list generated by reading the actual list, docs generated from runtime used to validate runtime, golden tests auto-regenerated on change) — a verifier requires at least one independent axis of truth.
entities: A VERIFIER REQUIRES AT LEAST ONE INDEPENDENT AXIS OF TRUTH

units.name: Behavioral Failure Forensics
units.text: When Claude introduces or lets a defect escape, runs an Agent Escape RCA classifying cause as retrieval failure, premature implementation, inherited-legitimacy bias, semantic duplicate blindness, scope blindness, completion bias, wrong authority, static-validation bias, happy-path fixation, historical-context omission, or evidence asymmetry — separate from product RCA.

units.name: Earliest Preventable Point
units.text: For each escaped defect, identifies the first point (intent parsing, repository discovery, capability resolution, planning, implementation, testing, Production Reality, Done) where it could have been prevented, enabling upstream correction.

units.name: No Repair Before Explaining Escape
units.text: Rule that, with practical limits for urgent incidents, state/failure/escape-mechanism evidence must be preserved before it's destroyed by the fix, so UFIA can actually learn.

units.name: Owner-Discovered Defect = Detection-System Incident
units.text: A deterministic defect found by the Owner after Done is not just a bug but a detection-system incident, requiring product repair, detection repair, and decision-process repair together; connects to HIC-OAR.
entities: OUR DETECTION/PREVENTION SYSTEM ALLOWED AN ESCAPE
units.canonical_key: owner discovered defect detection system incident

units.name: Agent Failure Observatory
units.text: Longitudinal telemetry of what percentage of defects originate from missing knowledge, retrieval, planning, implementation, governance, validation, discovery, tooling, or environment, feeding clear IFC investment priorities.

units.name: Governance-Induced Failure Detection
units.text: USIFB also audits CPP's own rules, since rule A + rule B can interact to produce pathological behavior (e.g. tension between bounded scope and opportunity discovery found in KIFS); governance itself becomes an anomaly-detection object.

units.name: Scope the Execution, Never the Observation
units.text: Observation can widen proportionally to look broadly, but execution stays bounded by ROI/risk/scope — preserves narrow execution while allowing wide observation.
entities: Scope the Execution, Never the Observation
units.canonical_key: scope the execution never the observation

units.name: Universal Inverted Funnel
units.text: UBC-integrated technique: narrow intent -> expand consequence space (interpretations, existing capabilities, dependencies, direct/indirect collaterals, lifecycle, user impact, integrity, failure space, unknown unknowns) -> evidence convergence (MUST ADDRESS/SHOULD ADDRESS/OBSERVE/NOT APPLICABLE/FUTURE OPPORTUNITY) -> narrow implementation.

units.name: Wide Thinking, Narrow Execution
units.text: Compact form of the Universal Inverted Funnel principle: a narrow request must never imply narrow reasoning, but also must never imply infinite execution.

units.name: Funnel width dynamic by mode
units.text: Sets funnel width per mode: EXECUTION MODE = small funnel, PLAN MODE = medium funnel, ULTRA-PLAN = wide funnel — avoids bureaucratizing every change.

units.name: Failure Hypothesis Library
units.text: Compresses hundreds/thousands of KIFS-style defect hypotheses into 18 superfamilies (Legitimacy, Completeness, Ownership, Identity, Lifecycle, Authority, Dependency & Interaction, Intent-Reality, Experience, Instrumentation, Propagation, Agent/Governance, Learning, Epistemic Integrity, Validity-by-Accident, Latent Contradiction, Recovery/Reversibility, Temporal Integrity) rather than converting each example into its own check.

units.name: Retrieval by applicability (USIFB)
units.text: UBC compiles only the hypothesis families relevant to a given feature's risk profile — a clipboard button needs none, a distributed-cache+async-persistence+migration feature activates authority/state-coherence/race/lifecycle/recovery/reconciliation/version-compatibility families.

units.name: Hypothesis Seeds structure
units.text: Each hypothesis-family pattern carries triggers, likely mechanism, affected surfaces, cheapest falsification, false-positive risks, historical evidence, confidence, siblings — not dogma, so the system reasons without assuming guilt.

units.name: Continuous Integrity Mode
units.text: Two-mode integrity checking: Transactional Integrity during each mission, and Continuous Integrity as periodic audits over drift, orphan state, expired compatibility, ownership, stale evidence, unexplained complexity, blind spots — critical for long-lived software.

units.name: Drift families universal
units.text: Universal drift taxonomy: Architecture Drift, Capability Drift, Ownership Drift, Lifecycle Drift, Config Drift, Dependency Drift, Experience Drift, Baseline Drift (new code stops inheriting current maturity).

units.name: Fresh Reconstruction Canary
units.text: Periodically builds a fresh instance from scratch; if historical production works but clean reconstruction fails, a hidden historical dependency is exposed — applicable to deployments, desktop apps, agent environments, plugins, infra.

units.name: Clean Install + Upgrade + Rollback Triad
units.text: For versioned software, tests clean install, upgrade from a representative historical version, and rollback/recovery when supported — most bugs live in the transitions.

units.name: What Only Works Because of History
units.text: Universal question that surfaces hidden bootstrap steps, manually created data, old migration assumptions, stale caches, undocumented operator rituals.
entities: What Only Works Because of History
units.canonical_key: what only works because of history

units.name: Operational Ritual Hunter
units.text: Detects unexplained recurring operator habits ("always do X twice", "always restart", "always ignore warning Y", "always copy this folder") which usually hide uninstitutionalized causal knowledge, and converts them to mechanism/automation or elimination.
units.parent: What Only Works Because of History

units.name: Shadow-System Hunter
units.text: Searches for shadow config, database, deploy path, permissions, state, scheduler, ownership — invisible parallel control planes that are a major bug source.

units.name: Effective-State Resolver
units.text: Never assumes a config file equals state; resolves the true precedence chain (defaults -> global -> environment -> project -> runtime override -> user/session context) as the operational truth, per prior reverse-engineering hard rule.

units.name: Authority Demonstrated by Direction of Control
units.text: A file is not canonical merely because it is named "canonical.json"; authority must be demonstrated by tracing what produces what and which consumer obeys which.
entities: Authority Demonstrated by Direction of Control
units.canonical_key: authority demonstrated by direction of control

units.name: Contradiction Mining
units.text: Compares intent, docs, architecture, source, tests, runtime, and agent claims to find contradictions (e.g. architecture says A canonical but runtime uses B) even when both individually "work."

units.name: Claim Integrity
units.text: Requires final reports (e.g. "production verified") to specify which production, which version, which scope, which timestamp, which evidence — preventing reports from accidentally laundering UNKNOWNs.

units.name: Evidence Freshness
units.text: A PASS ages: subsequent changes to code, config, dependency, environment, or deployment can make prior evidence STALE, invalidating the earlier PASS.

units.name: Stale-Success Detector
units.text: Flags old green tests, prior receipts, and pre-latest-change production smoke tests as stale, since PASS must be bound to the exact current state.

units.name: Metrology Integrity
units.text: USIFB turns its scrutiny on its own detectors, asking whether each has positive control, negative control, actually runs, and has a consumer for its findings.

units.name: Self-Auditing Integrity System
units.text: USIFB must audit not just software but also its own detectors, hypothesis library, router, governance, UKDL, and baselines, or it will accumulate its own bugs.
entities: KIFS UNIVERSAL MUST APPLY TO ITSELF

units.name: Learning Sediment Detection
units.text: Detects rules that have become obsolete or traps that no longer apply because the architecture that caused them no longer exists; feeds UKDL lifecycle.

units.name: Goodhart Defense
units.text: Guards against metrics like "anomalies found" (encourages noise) or "zero owner defects" (encourages reclassifying as subjective) becoming sole objectives; requires Reality + owner burden + defect escapes together.

units.name: Discovery ROI
units.text: Redefines audit success as net reduction in future defect cost and human attention rather than raw finding count — finding fewer things because prevention improved is a good outcome.
entities: NET REDUCTION IN FUTURE DEFECT COST AND HUMAN ATTENTION

units.name: Owner Burden as core metric
units.text: If USIFB surfaces 500 anomalies the Owner must classify, it has failed; findings must be prioritized by confidence, severity, systemic leverage, recurrence, cheap falsification, remediation cost.

units.name: Anomaly clustering causal
units.text: Groups many findings (e.g. 100 "unused file" findings) traced to one root cause (one broken generator) into a single IFC investment rather than 100 separate tasks.

units.name: Novel Defect Discovery Rate
units.text: Measures new problems found autonomously before the Owner does, indicating whether the frontier keeps expanding.

units.name: Owner-Discovered Defect Rate
units.text: Target trending toward zero for mechanical/deterministic defects (not for irreducible creative judgment).

units.name: Blind Spots Retired
units.text: Counts previously-unobservable surfaces that now have instrumentation, invariants, tests, provenance — measures epistemological coverage expansion.

units.name: Unknown-to-Known Conversion
units.text: Measures which important unknowns get economically resolved, rather than treating UNKNOWN itself as failure.

units.name: USIFB-driven Constitutive Baseline promotion
units.text: When USIFB discovers a new indispensable integrity dimension for a system family (e.g. resume correctness for agent runtimes after an incident), it can trigger Constitutive Baseline Ratchet promotion just as planned features do.

units.name: Universal Engineering Integrity Envelope
units.text: The combined inheritable envelope every new software gets: Construction, Production, Integrity, Failure Immunity, Foresight, Autonomy, Lifecycle, Learning.

units.name: Shared institutional primitive planes
units.text: Architectural decision to avoid mega-silo duplication: consolidate UCR, UFIA, HIC, IFC, UBC, USIFB onto shared owners — Institutional System Graph, Evidence & Knowledge Plane, Universal Evaluation Plane, Baseline & Policy Plane, Construction/Failure/Intervention Event Stream, Institutional Flywheel Controller — with KIFS universal as analysis modes over those primitives.

units.name: Institutional System Graph
units.text: Shared plane holding provenance, dependencies, ownership, capabilities, lifecycle for all institutional systems.

units.name: Evidence & Knowledge Plane
units.text: Shared plane combining Vault + UKDL + confidence + lineage.

units.name: Universal Evaluation Plane
units.text: Shared plane for tests, adversaries, counterfactuals, metamorphic tests.

units.name: Baseline & Policy Plane
units.text: Shared plane combining UBC, applicability, and enforcement.

units.name: Construction/Failure/Intervention Event Stream
units.text: Shared observed-evidence event stream feeding the institutional planes.

units.name: Baseline Capsule extended contract set
units.text: Post-USIFB Baseline Capsule adds Legitimacy Contract, Ownership Contract, Completeness Contract, Forbidden-State Contract, Provenance Contract, Lifecycle Contract, Failure Hypotheses, Latent Contradictions, Blind-Spot Plan, Foresight Adversaries to the UBC's compiled output.

units.name: Pre-mission USIFB pipeline
units.text: Pipeline: intent -> inverted funnel -> reality scan -> system family -> inherited baseline -> legitimacy model -> ownership -> capabilities -> historical failure families -> validity-by-accident search -> latent contradictions -> known blind spots -> capsule.

units.name: During-mission incremental recompile
units.text: On each diff, USIFB re-asks legitimacy/ownership/duplicate-provider/lifecycle-change/generated-source-boundary/new-assumption/new-forbidden-state/new-blind-spot/new-historical-residue questions and incrementally recompiles the capsule.

units.name: Before-Done Challenge set
units.text: Pre-Done gate beyond green tests: Integrity Challenge, Completeness Challenge, Ownership Challenge, Reality Challenge, Validity Challenge, Unknown Challenge, Adversarial Challenge.

units.name: Foresight Delta
units.text: Post-mission output measuring what new ways of being wrong CPP can now recognize, added alongside Product/Capability/Immunity/Autonomy/Baseline deltas.

units.name: Six mission capital types
units.text: Each mission now produces Product Capital, Capability Capital, Immunity Capital, Autonomy Capital, Baseline Capital, and Foresight Capital.

units.name: Foresight Capital
units.text: Persistent institutional capacity to suspect, predict, falsify, or detect a future failure class it previously would not have known to look for.

units.name: Foresight Compound Rate
units.text: Measures how much each incident/construction expands the future-detectable defect space, rewarding future findings rather than rule count.

units.name: Universal Unknown-Unknown Frontier
units.text: Maintains Known Known Failures, Known Unknowns, Hypothesized Unknowns, and Blind Domains, with the goal of moving the frontier.

units.name: SOFTWARE EPISTEMIC QUALITY
units.text: Thesis that beyond raising software quality, USIFB raises the system's capacity to know what exists, why, where, who's in charge, what evidence proves it, what assumptions support it, what it might be hiding, and what remains unknown — a "green" system can still be fragile without this.

units.name: A SYSTEM IS NOT MATURE MERELY BECAUSE ITS KNOWN REQUIREMENTS PASS
units.text: Constitutional law that maturity requires proportional capability to discover unjustified state, hidden coupling, latent contradictions, blind spots, and plausible unknown failure modes — not just passing known requirements.
entities: A SYSTEM IS NOT MATURE MERELY BECAUSE ITS KNOWN REQUIREMENTS PASS
units.canonical_key: a system is not mature merely because its known requirements pass

units.name: EVERY OWNER-DISCOVERED DETERMINISTIC DEFECT MUST EXPAND THE INSTITUTION'S ABILITY TO DISCOVER THAT DEFECT FAMILY
units.text: Constitutional law requiring every owner-discovered deterministic defect to expand detection capability for that defect family and its siblings before the next occurrence.
entities: EVERY OWNER-DISCOVERED DETERMINISTIC DEFECT MUST EXPAND THE INSTITUTION'S ABILITY TO DISCOVER THAT DEFECT FAMILY
units.canonical_key: every owner discovered deterministic defect must expand the institution s ability to discover that defect family

units.name: NORMALITY DOES NOT PROVE LEGITIMACY
units.text: The most KIFS-flavored constitutional law: normality does not prove legitimacy, existence does not prove necessity, success does not prove correctness, absence of observed failure does not prove safety without proven exposure and observability.

units.name: Fable 5 World Demo
units.text: A donor corpus (github.com/Braffolk/fable5-world-demo) — an ~21,000-line strict-TypeScript WebGPU project built almost entirely by an autonomous agent, whose 96-commit history and near-1000-line STATUS.md document empirical debugging, autonomous metrology, falsification and agent self-correction rather than 3D graphics techniques.

units.name: STATUS.md operational memory
units.text: LAAS's source-of-truth continuity document with a rehydration protocol, current state, next steps, diagnosis logs, and measurements, explicitly instructing the agent not to restart from scratch and to update after every significant step.

units.name: Project Operational Memory / Knowledge Vault / UKDL three-layer memory
units.text: Universalizes LAAS's STATUS.md into a three-layer memory model: Project Operational Memory (what's happening in this system), Knowledge Vault (why concrete incidents occurred), UKDL (distilled universal principles).
entities: Project Operational Memory / Knowledge Vault / UKDL three-layer memory
units.canonical_key: project operational memory knowledge vault ukdl three layer memory

units.name: INSTALLED REALITY > MODEL MEMORY
units.text: Before using an unfamiliar API (e.g. three/TSL), verify against the installed implementation and pinned-version types rather than trusting model memory — applies to SDKs, frameworks, CLIs, APIs, compilers, dependency versions.

units.name: WHEN BEHAVIOR IS CHEAPLY PROBEABLE, OBSERVE IT
units.text: Hard rule that runtime/documentation-uncertain semantics (depth conventions, camera behavior, TSL stack semantics, buffer indexing, shadow behavior) should be probed in shader/runtime rather than reasoned from generic docs.
entities: WHEN BEHAVIOR IS CHEAPLY PROBEABLE, OBSERVE IT
units.canonical_key: when behavior is cheaply probeable observe it

units.name: DIAGNOSTIC CAPABILITY CREATION IS PART OF IMPLEMENTATION
units.text: LAAS progressively built its own diagnostic tools (screenshot harness, comparison tool, pixel sampler, GPU profiler, ablation switches, LOD debug views, hydrology views, class-debug coloring, face orientation debugging, horizon/cloud-lag/pointer-lock probes) instead of waiting for perfect external tooling; elevated to a universal law that building the needed instrument is part of implementation.
entities: DIAGNOSTIC CAPABILITY CREATION IS PART OF IMPLEMENTATION
units.canonical_key: diagnostic capability creation is part of implementation

units.name: Observability capital from hard bugs
units.text: UFIA-EBF principle that a difficult bug should buy a new permanent diagnostic instrument (e.g. a frame-locked probe eliminating temporal noise), not just a regression test — the instrument remains available for future sibling bugs.

units.name: BUGFIXING IS HYPOTHESIS TESTING
units.text: LAAS's systematic hypothesis -> isolate -> ablate -> measure -> accept/refute loop (e.g. isolating the horizon-black bug to postprocessing, then AO, then two specific mechanisms) elevated to universal doctrine over guess-and-change debugging.

units.name: NEGATIVE EXPERIMENT MEMORY
units.text: Preserves refuted hypotheses (e.g. a plausible fix for the water-shards bug that was implemented, tested, found not to change the result, and reverted uncommitted) as vault entries (hypothesis, evidence, experiment, result, refutation) so Claude never re-pays the same false path.

units.name: A CHANGE THAT DOES NOT IMPROVE ITS CLAIMED TARGET MUST NOT SURVIVE BY INERTIA
units.text: UKDL law that a candidate fix which doesn't improve the phenomenon and has no independently verified value must be reverted, not kept because work was already done (no sunk-cost survival).
entities: A CHANGE THAT DOES NOT IMPROVE ITS CLAIMED TARGET MUST NOT SURVIVE BY INERTIA
units.canonical_key: a change that does not improve its claimed target must not survive by inertia

units.name: Do not modify the component most visually associated with the symptom
units.text: Requires demonstrating which subsystem has causal power via ablation before fixing (e.g. testing atmosphere/shadows/water/AO candidates for the black horizon) rather than fixing the component that merely looks associated with the symptom.
entities: Do not modify the component most visually associated with the symptom
units.canonical_key: do not modify the component most visually associated with the symptom

units.name: STACKED ROOT CAUSE MODEL
units.text: A defect can have multiple simultaneous root causes (the cloud-lag bug had three: incorrect sky velocity, one-frame-stale camera uniforms, incorrect geometry velocity) — fixing only one leaves the system still broken; UFIA must model R1+R2+R3 stacks rather than forcing a single cause.

units.name: Residual testing after root-cause removal
units.text: After eliminating one cause, requires retesting to confirm the symptom is actually gone (not merely improved) before declaring closure, since partial improvement often causes premature stop.
units.canonical_key: residual testing after root cause removal

units.name: CONTRASTIVE DEBUGGING
units.text: Localizes a "half works" bug by asking what differs between working and failing cases (e.g. terrain casts shadows, vegetation doesn't; stones do, trees don't) rather than bisecting whole pipeline layers — generalizes to users, tenants, requests, machines, browsers, datasets, workers, configurations.

units.name: clsdbg debug view
units.text: A LAAS-built specialized debug view that flat-colored vegetation classes, converting hours of guessing about "dark slabs" into rapid identification; universalized to route-coloring, provenance overlays, state-owner inspectors, cache-source inspectors, agent decision traces, data lineage views.
units.parent: DIAGNOSTIC CAPABILITY CREATION IS PART OF IMPLEMENTATION

units.name: Causal-structure observability
units.text: Observability should represent not just "something happened" but which path, subsystem, state, input, derived value, transformation — reducing Human Debugging Burden.

units.name: NO REPAIR BEFORE PRESERVING THE INCIDENT
units.text: LAAS committed bug reports (screenshot + candidate diagnosis) before fixing, for both the horizon and cloud-lag bugs — universalized as a UFIA/KIFS rule.
entities: NO REPAIR BEFORE PRESERVING THE INCIDENT
units.canonical_key: no repair before preserving the incident

units.name: Owner report as high-value evidence
units.text: Owner reports are treated as high-value evidence rather than presumed wrong (the log confirms the user was right about which surface was failing on the black-horizon bug), elevating HIC-OAR to investigate why the machine didn't see it first.
units.canonical_key: owner report as high value evidence

units.name: Human perception is evidence; human causal explanation is a hypothesis
units.text: Separates the Owner's observed phenomenon (treated as evidence) from the Owner's proposed mechanism (treated as an unproven hypothesis) — the system, not the human, determines mechanism.
entities: Human perception is evidence; human causal explanation is a hypothesis
units.canonical_key: human perception is evidence human causal explanation is a hypothesis

units.name: Generalized reproducer construction
units.text: Built a systematic reproducer (an 8-yaw sweep plus sightline search) for a bug only visible at certain low-altitude grazing sightlines that regular bookmarks missed, generalizing user report -> generalized reproducer -> parameter sweep, creating Neighborhood Regression Coverage.

units.name: Representative happy viewpoints can systematically miss geometric boundaries
units.text: Canonical bookmarks/happy-path viewpoints did not capture certain bugs; generalizes to standard test users, canonical tenants, median payloads, normal network conditions not constituting exhaustive coverage.
entities: Representative happy viewpoints can systematically miss geometric boundaries
units.canonical_key: representative happy viewpoints can systematically miss geometric boundaries

units.name: Boundary/edge-space search activation
units.text: UBC could activate boundary search automatically when a feature contains thresholds, geometrical bounds, paging, LOD, time transitions, numeric interpolation, capacity limits.

units.name: Automatic adversarial sweep generation
units.text: Testing could auto-generate sweeps across all orientations, min/max values, threshold ± epsilon, several frame rates, viewport sizes, lifecycle states, rather than relying on manual prompt enumeration.

units.name: STATIC CORRECTNESS DOES NOT PROVE TEMPORAL CORRECTNESS
units.text: The cloud-lag bug could not be reproduced with a static setPose since it only appeared during interactive movement and real update order; generalizes to animations, async state, streaming, event systems, distributed state, UI, agents.
entities: STATIC CORRECTNESS DOES NOT PROVE TEMPORAL CORRECTNESS
units.canonical_key: static correctness does not prove temporal correctness

units.name: Sequence tests requirement for temporal systems
units.text: Two matching frames do not prove smooth transition, absence of lag, absence of stale state, absence of flicker, or absence of accumulation bugs — temporal systems need sequence tests, not snapshot tests.
entities: Sequence tests requirement for temporal systems
units.parent: STATIC CORRECTNESS DOES NOT PROVE TEMPORAL CORRECTNESS
units.canonical_key: sequence tests requirement for temporal systems

units.name: HEADLESS/CI PASS MAY NOT SATISFY INTERACTIVE CLAIMS
units.text: LAAS documented that static headless shots didn't reproduce the user environment (different DPR, resizing, continuous motion, temporal history) and required verifying both before declaring certain lighting issues fixed.
entities: HEADLESS/CI PASS MAY NOT SATISFY INTERACTIVE CLAIMS
units.canonical_key: headless ci pass may not satisfy interactive claims

units.name: REPRODUCE THE CLAIMED ENVIRONMENT BEFORE OPTIMIZING THE CLAIMED PROBLEM
units.text: When headless benchmarks measured 33-45fps but the user observed 10-15fps, the plan shifted to reproducing the real viewport first, rather than trusting synthetic benchmark authority over the real environment.
entities: REPRODUCE THE CLAIMED ENVIRONMENT BEFORE OPTIMIZING THE CLAIMED PROBLEM
units.canonical_key: reproduce the claimed environment before optimizing the claimed problem

units.name: Benchmark environment-identity requirement
units.text: A performance result without hardware, resolution, DPR, thermal state, runtime, workload metadata is weak evidence; UBC should require proportional metadata.
units.parent: REPRODUCE THE CLAIMED ENVIRONMENT BEFORE OPTIMIZING THE CLAIMED PROBLEM

units.name: Thermal state as explicit confound
units.text: LAAS measured up to ~50% cross-run variation on a hot M1 Max and adopted ABAB pairs/in-session averages; generalizes to controlling thermal state, caching, warmup, JIT, network, background load in any benchmark.

units.name: Measurement methodology as baseline
units.text: Elevates measurement methodology itself (not just the performance target) to part of the baseline — metrology infrastructure.

units.name: Metrics have semantic contracts
units.text: A metric is valid only if what it actually measures is known — headless FPS may not represent GPU throughput because CPU can submit ahead, and pass timestamps can include dependency stalls; each metric needs a semantic contract (e.g. gpu-pass-time is encoder span, not marginal cost) to avoid Goodharting.
entities: FPS is not a naive metric

units.name: PROFILER COST != CAUSAL COST
units.text: A pass appeared expensive in timestamps but removing it barely changed wall time due to overlap/stalls; performance changes must be validated by ablation (remove/disable, measure whole-system delta), not profiler numbers alone.

units.name: Performance optimization as causal science
units.text: Pipeline: instrument -> rank suspected whales -> ablate -> optimize -> measure wall impact -> verify quality, replacing vague "optimize loops" guidance.

units.name: FIX BOTTLENECK -> RECOMPUTE BOTTLENECK
units.text: After GPU-bound optimizations, CPU submit became the new binding constraint; connects to IFC — never keep optimizing the previous bottleneck after it moves.

units.name: Performance architecture quality floor
units.text: The Owner forbade reducing draw distance, density, visible detail, or resolution to hit performance targets; optimization must respect hard visual-quality constraints rather than trading latency at any price.

units.name: Pareto proof requirement for optimizations
units.text: After each performance change: compile, visual diff, benchmark, commit with numbers — a gain is only promoted if it doesn't buy a critical regression, aligning with IFC.

units.name: Performance commit proof receipts
units.text: LAAS commits carried empirical values (e.g. "shadow cache: -4ms", "depth prepass: -10ms"); CPP should require before/after/environment/quality-delta/confidence receipts for significant optimizations.

units.name: Performance regressions as first-class failures
units.text: Performance regressions are not secondary bugs, especially when a runtime requirement treats performance as part of correctness.
units.canonical_key: performance regressions as first class failures

units.name: Visual/UX regression baseline
units.text: LAAS compares captures against references, requires writing the ten most relevant visual differences, fixing the top three, and re-rendering before closing a phase — visual/UX quality gets a regression baseline like correctness.

units.name: REFERENCE-DELTA LOOP
units.text: Universal loop for judging output quality against a golden reference rather than "looks acceptable" — applies to UI, product design, emails, dashboards, reports, generated assets, not only 3D graphics; the brief forbids lowering the target for convenience.

units.name: Impact-based correction ordering
units.text: Quality gaps should be prioritized by perceptual/business impact rather than technical ease, per LAAS ranking top visual deltas and fixing the top three first; connects to IFC.

units.name: An unfinished stub cannot satisfy a completion claim
units.text: The brief treats any leftover stub or unfinished marker in a closed phase as failure; universalized (with applicability) as a completion law aligned with the Reality Contract.
entities: An unfinished stub cannot satisfy a completion claim
No unfinished markers in a closed phase
units.canonical_key: an unfinished stub cannot satisfy a completion claim

units.name: DEVIATION IS A STATE, NOT A SECRET
units.text: When an item proves infeasible, the nearest feasible alternative plus an explicit deviation record is required — never silently marked "done."
entities: DEVIATION IS A STATE, NOT A SECRET
units.canonical_key: deviation is a state not a secret

units.name: Implementation debt vs accepted deviation distinction
units.text: Institutional honesty requires distinguishing unresolved implementation debt from a formally accepted deviation.
entities: Implementation debt vs accepted deviation distinction
units.parent: DEVIATION IS A STATE, NOT A SECRET
units.canonical_key: implementation debt vs accepted deviation distinction

units.name: Human perceptual judgment reservation
units.text: LAAS reserved rare human input for things hard to judge from static output (wind feel, camera bob, cloud motion, water taste) — a working example of HIC-OAR: machine handles mechanical evidence, human handles high-level perceptual judgment.

units.name: Subjective-to-measurable conversion
units.text: A human observation (e.g. cloud lag) is progressively converted into instrumentation (frame-locked measurement), reducing future need for human intervention and moving the HIC-OAR human boundary upward.

units.name: Owner correction to structural constraint
units.text: An Owner-reported bug class (e.g. wind phase-explosion from shared tempo) was eliminated "by construction" via redesign rather than a tweak; establishes a priority order documentation < test < validator < primitive < architecture, connecting to UFIA.

units.name: TIME-BASED BEHAVIOR MUST NOT SILENTLY DEPEND ON EXECUTION RATE UNLESS INTENDED
