units.name: Existing Wii engineering systems inventory
units.text: Enumerates pre-existing KobiiSports Resort systems (Wii Boot Determinism Engine, Wii Runtime Telemetry Layer, Wii Frontend State Machine & Input Routing Engine, Wii Frontend Baseline Preservation Engine, Wii Frontend Layout Lifecycle Verification Engine, Wii Motion OS, Universal Reference Assimilation & Production Reconstruction Fabric, Research System, Wii Production Intelligence Platform, KADOS) and concepts (One-Boot Root Cause Protocol, Runtime Digital Twin, Differential Boot Intelligence, Control Boot System, Hardware Truth Network, self-evolving diagnostic benchmarks, mutation benchmarks, capability graphs, Architecture Truth, Capability Gap Engine, benchmark difficulty tiers).

units.name: Zero-Boot Engineering
units.text: Evidence-cost hierarchy (static evidence -> contract/property tests -> host simulation -> model-based testing -> Dolphin/instrumented emulator -> calibrated Wii Digital Twin -> hardware boot -> player reality) reserving real hardware boots for questions only hardware can answer.

units.name: No Boot Without Expected Information Gain
units.text: Constitutional law that before every real hardware boot, Claude must articulate live hypotheses, discriminating evidence, needed instrumentation, expected outcomes per hypothesis, and a fallback plan; a boot that only reports "still black" is a diagnostic-architecture failure, not an acceptable result.
entities: No Boot Without Expected Information Gain
units.canonical_key: no boot without expected information gain

units.name: Hardware Experiment Compiler
units.text: Compiles Mission State, Failure Hypotheses, Previous Boots, Architecture Graph, and Available Probes into an optimal experiment plan before each boot; after the boot, normalizes/compares artifacts and performs a causal update feeding the next experiment — turning many boots into a Bayesian-like uncertainty-reduction sequence.

units.name: One-Run Root Cause
units.text: Generalizes One-Boot Root Cause to any expensive execution (Wii boot -> production run, web session -> browser run, agent mission -> agent run, distributed incident -> trace/replay) under the discipline that every failed run must drastically reduce the remaining causal space.

units.name: Retail/Reference Reconstruction
units.text: Elevates existing retail games (or, universally, old versions/reference implementations/competitor behavior/protocol clients/legacy systems/known-good binaries) into executable specifications via Reference -> Behavioral Contract Reconstruction -> Minimal Replica -> Differential Validation -> Controlled Extension.
units.parent: Universal Reference Assimilation & Production Reconstruction Fabric

units.name: Retail-vs-Custom Differential Runtime
units.text: Runs a retail reference and a custom reconstruction side by side, comparing scene transitions, GX state, memory, resources, input, timing, audio, save, lifecycle, output to find the first observable divergence rather than guessing where the bug is.

units.name: Architectural Truth Compiler
units.text: Before modifying retail/Kamek code, reconstructs producers, consumers, ownership, lifecycle, hidden contracts, state transitions, memory obligations, call boundaries so implementation targets an architectural model rather than isolated symbols; universalizes to legacy code, microservices, APIs, stateful applications, agents.

units.name: ARTIFACT-CONTEXT IDENTITY
units.text: No symbol, offset, trace, benchmark, test expectation, or contract may be consumed without being bound to its artifact identity, version, region/build, hash, and environment — "works in v1.2" does not mean "works in v1.3."

units.name: Evidence-Bound Reverse Engineering
units.text: Every recovered fact must be tagged OBSERVED, INFERRED, VERIFIED, HARDWARE-CONFIRMED, CONFLICTING, or UNKNOWN and never mixed — a mislabeled fact can contaminate weeks of reverse engineering; a claim must never exceed the confidence of its weakest material evidence.

units.name: Specification proportional to consequence
units.text: Formalizes only high-consequence surfaces (boot, scene lifecycle, frontend transitions, resource lifecycle, save/load, network protocol, GX resource ownership) using contracts/property-stateful testing/typestate/selective model checking/mutation testing — avoiding "formal methods theater."

units.name: Wii Failure Mutation Genome
units.text: Domain-specific mutation set targeting real Wii bug classes (scene omitted, resource initialized late, GX state not restored, wrong region symbol, invalid lifecycle transition, MEM1 exhaustion, stale pointer, input event consumed twice, save partial, timing boundary, wrong frontend layout lifecycle) used to measure Defect Sensitivity rather than raw test count.

units.name: Self-Evolving Benchmark Genome for Wii
units.text: Per-capability benchmark families (Boot Intelligence, Frontend Intelligence, Motion Intelligence, GX Intelligence) that, once saturated, move to the Regression Vault while the Difficulty Engine creates a new frontier — the KMEIP pattern applied to Wii.
units.parent: CPP Software Engineering Evolution & Intelligence Platform
units.canonical_key: self evolving benchmark genome for wii

units.name: Benchmark saturation criteria
units.text: A benchmark is only considered saturated (not merely 100%-passing) given repeated pass, real-defect sensitivity, mutation-kill evidence, multiple environments, historical bugs, adversarial variants, and low discrimination against stronger candidates — preventing benchmark gaming.

units.name: Wii bug-to-permanent-benchmark pipeline
units.text: Pipeline: black screen -> preserve evidence -> reproducer -> causal isolation -> violated invariant -> exact regression -> failure family -> mutation -> benchmark -> UKDL -> applicable baseline -> sibling scan -> future prediction, matching KMEIP's Failure->Evidence->Root Cause->Invariant->Benchmark->Regression->Knowledge->Prevention trajectory.
units.canonical_key: wii bug to permanent benchmark pipeline

units.name: Observability Difficulty Engine
units.text: Benchmarks the diagnostic probes themselves (how many bugs can current telemetry discriminate, which regions remain black boxes) and increases instrumentation resolution wherever many bugs land in the same unresolved region.

units.name: OBSERVABILITY HAS A BUDGET
units.text: Because Wii hardware is limited, every probe is evaluated by Diagnostic Information Gain / Runtime Cost rather than "log everything."

units.name: Runtime Flight Recorder
units.text: A compact debug-build recorder holding latest semantic transitions, last safe checkpoint, resource state changes, critical errors, memory pressure, input lifecycle — read on crash/hang instead of relying on what was visible on screen.

units.name: Hardware Truth Network
units.text: Aggregates system environment/behavior/timing/reproducibility across Wii hardware profiles to distinguish universal bugs from model-specific, IOS/cIOS/environment, USB-path, or resource-pressure issues, making compatibility non-anecdotal with enough runs.

units.name: TWIN != TRUTH
units.text: A Wii Digital Twin is only valid in domains where it is calibrated against hardware; every hardware-vs-twin discrepancy becomes a Twin Divergence Incident that improves the twin — a twin is only valid while it holds recent calibration, a fidelity metric, and a declared boundary of use.

units.name: Twin Divergence Incident
units.text: Formal incident record for each observed hardware-vs-twin discrepancy, used to improve twin fidelity.

units.name: Simulator Coverage Map
units.text: Per-capability matrix (Host/Dolphin/Twin/Hardware strength: pure state machine, GX behavior, MEM1/MEM2 pressure, Wiimote behavior, USB loader chain, player feel) telling UBC which evidence path to apply, with player feel marked human-authority-only.

units.name: CHEAPEST TRUSTWORTHY EVIDENCE ROUTE
units.text: Escalates from static evidence to emulator only when unresolved, and to hardware directly when that capability has a historical emulator-hardware divergence — the system learns the cheapest trustworthy route rather than either starting at hardware or getting stuck in simulation.

units.name: Deterministic Build-to-Hardware pipeline
units.text: Demonstrable chain source commit -> build -> DOL -> injection/package -> WBFS -> USB artifact -> boot, hashed at every boundary, eliminating "am I really testing the build I think I am" — universalizes to software supply chain.

units.name: Production Artifact Identity
units.text: All hardware evidence must bind to exact artifact lineage, not a vague label like "new KSR build," making boots comparable.

units.name: Hardware Feature Bisect
units.text: When a candidate release bundles many changes, produces discriminating builds using the architecture graph, failure hypotheses, dependency graph, and feature flags to choose maximum-information-gain partitions instead of blind git-bisect.

units.name: Semantic Bisection
units.text: More powerful than commit bisection — asks which capability (GX resource management, frontend lifecycle, persistence, input) introduced a divergence, further reducing boot count.

units.name: GEX44 as Player/Hardware Reality Cortex
units.text: Repositions GEX44 from final-QA gate to a presence throughout development, benchmarking, failure investigation, and promotion, evaluating not just function correctness but input feel, visual fidelity, audio, motion, menu behavior, latency, player-facing truth — a feature is not promoted merely because the state machine passed.
units.canonical_key: gex44 as player hardware reality cortex

units.name: Sensory Benchmarks
units.text: Formalizes hard-to-measure sensory attributes (motion feel, latency, animation feel, audio sync, visual transitions) that, once partially objectified, generalize to games, UI, interactive software, robotics.

units.name: Human-to-Instrument conversion (Wii)
units.text: Converts a human report ("this swing fails sometimes") into an input trace, timing envelope, and missed-swing benchmark — HIC-OAR's human judgement -> diagnostic instrument -> regression pipeline applied to Wii motion.

units.name: Wii Production Capability Genome
units.text: Set of shared capabilities (boot, frontend, input, GX, assets, audio, save, loading, scene lifecycle, error recovery, telemetry, packaging, hardware certification) every production Wii game inherits, so new games only need deep work on genuine game novelty.

units.name: Certified Wii Engineering Primitives
units.text: Proven-many-times Wii capabilities (safe GX resource lifecycle, scene transition primitive, persistent-state primitive, runtime telemetry primitive, region-safe symbol resolution, input routing primitive, hardware evidence packaging) that graduate feature -> reusable capability -> certified primitive -> Wii baseline, inherited automatically via the Constitutive Baseline Ratchet.

units.name: Wii Golden Path SDK
units.text: A new Wii game starts not from a blank repo or giant starter project but a compiled bundle of production bootstrap, evidence pipeline, telemetry hooks, benchmarks, state model, artifact provenance, hardware harness, and UKDL pack — only the applicable capabilities.

units.name: Game-Class Baselines
units.text: Per-genre baseline (e.g. Wii Sports-like title requiring motion, local multiplayer, sports hub) layered on top of the shared Wii Production Capability Genome.

units.name: Discovery materiality levels (D0-D7)
units.text: A seven-level ladder (D0 Raw Discovery through D7 Baseline Capability/Immunity) used to classify how far a captured event should be processed, from a bare observed event up to something enforced by test/gate/primitive.

units.name: Bug Closure Gate
units.text: A 16-question checklist (reproduced? artifact identified? cause? invariant broken? fix eliminates cause or symptom? regression exists? siblings? exposure scan? Vault updated? UKDL evaluated? baseline promotion evaluated? benchmark/detector/primitive evaluated? why did it escape? avoided human dependency? Production Reality demonstrates closure? remaining unknowns?) that must be answered (proportionally) before closing a material bug.

units.name: Triple separation: Evidence, Interpretation, Doctrine
units.text: A constitutional separation ensuring "what happened" (Evidence), "why we believe it happened" (Interpretation), and "what should be done" (Doctrine) are never merged, so that a change in interpretation never destroys evidence.

units.name: Bug Inverted Funnel
units.text: The specific 10-step causal-expansion-then-compression sequence (concrete bug → causal expansion → consequence expansion → sibling expansion → mechanism expansion → cross-domain expansion → unknown-unknown/latent-contradiction search → evidence convergence → compression → minimal causal fix → institutionalization) replacing the naive bug→cause→fix→regression→UKDL shortcut.

units.name: Funnel quality metrics (Recall/Precision/Premature Convergence Rate/etc.)
units.text: A set of measures for the funnel itself: Funnel Recall, Funnel Precision, Premature Convergence Rate, Brainstorm-to-Evidence Ratio, Owner Missing-Branch Rate, Compression Quality.
units.canonical_key: funnel quality metrics recall precision premature convergence rate etc

units.name: KIFS Recursive Causal Funnel Compiler
units.text: The evolution of KIFM into a "Funnel-of-Funnels" — twelve sequential sub-funnels (Symptom, Mechanism, Contrast, Propagation, Sibling, Temporal, Composition, Epistemic, Agent-Escape, Foresight, Cross-Domain, Institutionalization) that transform any intent, change, bug or anomaly into the minimally sufficient space of hypotheses, consequences, contradictions and future states before permitting a narrow decision.

units.name: Assumption Explosion Engine
units.text: Extracts implicit assumptions in an implementation (single writer, one instance, stable ordering, etc.) and performs "assumption inversion" — asking what happens if each ceases to be true — to generate hypotheses brainstorming would miss.

units.name: Assumption Interaction Engine
units.text: A more powerful version of assumption analysis that looks for combinations (A+B+C) where each assumption individually remains true but their conjunction produces a latent contradiction that has not yet manifested.

units.name: Triadic Contradiction Mining
units.text: Extends contradiction search beyond pairs to three-way (A+B+C) combinations, since many complex defects (e.g., retry + side effect + acknowledgement-after-commit → duplication under timeout) are ternary.

units.name: Novelty Reserve
units.text: Reserves roughly 20% of funnel expansion effort for taxonomy-free discovery, where a reviewer with deliberately fewer categories asks "what seems strange even without a name for it," preserving true unknown-unknown discovery capacity.

units.name: Funnel Branch
units.text: A machine-manageable candidate explanation/risk/question with fields (trigger, mechanism, evidence required, cheapest falsification, blast radius, potential siblings, confidence, source, cost) and a lifecycle status (CONFIRMED/REFUTED/LOW-PROBABILITY/NOT_APPLICABLE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE/DEFERRED).

units.name: Falsification-first routing / Information Gain Planner
units.text: Ranks candidate branches/experiments by discriminatory power divided by cost, so the cheapest experiment eliminating the most hypothesis mass is run first (e.g., choosing which Wii boot distinguishes the most theories).
units.canonical_key: falsification first routing information gain planner

units.name: Subtraction Funnel
units.text: A funnel dedicated to asking "what no longer has the right to exist after this change?" — covering supersession, cleanup, migration residue, old tests/docs/permissions/metrics/agents/gates.

units.name: Boundary Funnel
units.text: Asks what boundaries (process, thread, service, server, world, user, tenant, environment, privilege, filesystem, network, trust) a bug or change crosses, since defects often occur when correct data crosses the wrong boundary.

units.name: Authority Funnel
units.text: For each important fact, asks who can read/write/override/invalidate/restore/supersede it; inability to answer produces an Epistemic Integrity Finding.

units.name: Representation Funnel
units.text: Asks what transformations exist between the multiple representations of the same thing (source, cache, DB, UI, generated artifact, runtime object, log, API response), which is authoritative, and whether they can diverge.

units.name: Temporal Funnel / Long-horizon funnel
units.text: Models the full lifecycle (creation, initialization, active, idle, restart, upgrade, migration, failure, recovery, shutdown, retirement) and long horizons (10 seconds, after restart, after a week, after a version, when provider changes, when owner disappears, when data grows, when nodes scale) rather than only "works now."

units.name: Scale Inversion
units.text: Systematically inverts cardinality (1→2, 10→10,000, many→0/1) to find defects hiding in singleton assumptions at cardinality transitions.

units.name: Symmetry Breaking Funnel
units.text: Asks what variation (different player, locale, orientation, node, map, version) breaks the symmetry of current tests, since overly symmetric fixtures can hide bugs (a Fable-derived lesson).

units.name: Masking-Layer Funnel
units.text: Asks what fallback/tolerance/retry/default/cache might be making an invalid state look functional, and proposes validating with masking layers disabled (strict parser, fail-fast, cache disabled).

units.name: Contrafactual/Reverse Counterfactual Reconstruction
units.text: Asks (a) what would not exist if the system were rebuilt today from intent + current baseline (revealing historical anomalies) and (b) what hidden capability disappears if an apparently redundant piece is removed (Negative Necessity Testing), preventing destructive cleanup.

units.name: Causal Blast Radius / Prevention Ascension Funnel
units.text: After a root cause, builds the full blast radius of dependents (files, modules, services, projects, families, baselines, primitives, tests, knowledge) and then determines the earliest level (production→integration→test→static→planning→API contract→certified primitive→architectural impossibility) at which the mechanism can be killed.
entities: Causal Blast Radius / Prevention Ascension Funnel
units.canonical_key: causal blast radius prevention ascension funnel

units.name: Escape Funnel / Meta-Escape Funnel
units.text: Investigates why a bug escaped (missing observation, wrong context retrieval, false evidence, agent anchoring, etc.) and, more deeply, why KIFS/RCFC itself failed to ask the right question (missing branch family, bad router, taxonomy blindness, premature compression).

units.name: Funnel Genome
units.text: A named, generalizable record of which branches would have been necessary to anticipate a given owner-discovered defect (e.g., "Reuse/Provider Resolution Funnel Genome" from multiple duplication incidents); genomes can compose (e.g., Cache Integrity Genome + Distributed State Genome → reconciliation branches).

units.name: Foresight Horizon
units.text: Classifies plausible future failures as IMMINENT, ENABLED, LATENT, or SPECULATIVE so the backlog isn't filled with science fiction.

units.name: Contradiction Graph / Assumption Registry
units.text: A graph of facts, invariants, assumptions and forbidden states enabling queries like "A contradicts B" or "A+B enable forbidden C"; each assumption carries scope, evidence, owner, confidence, validity conditions, consumers, and can expire.

units.name: Invariant Synthesis
units.text: After multiple incidents, searches for a common deep invariant (e.g., "CLAIMED STATE MUST NOT ADVANCE BEYOND VERIFIED EFFECT STATE") that compresses several failure families into one.

units.name: Funnel Compression Engine
units.text: As the system learns, converts many explicit branches into fewer deep invariants, raising Institutional Knowledge while lowering Context Required — mirroring UKDL's compression behavior.

units.name: Funnel Branch Budget
units.text: A per-mission budget (context, tools, experiments, time/compute) assigned by IFC/UBC, larger for critical high-uncertainty missions and near-zero for trivial deterministic ones; reserves a small "surprise search" percentage even for known missions.

units.name: Branch Value Function
units.text: A conceptual scoring formula (expected severity × plausibility × blast radius × information value × institutional leverage ÷ investigation cost) used to decide investigation order; Systemic Leverage gives priority to branches that could reveal a broken universal primitive.

units.name: Funnel output compilation (Active Constraints/Risks/Unknowns/Experiments/Deferred Branches)
units.text: The compact final output format of a funnel pass, avoiding a sprawling brainstorming document; execution stays a "smallest coherent delta" regardless of how many improvements were discovered.
units.canonical_key: funnel output compilation active constraints risks unknowns experiments deferred branches

units.name: Funnel Reopen Trigger / Counterexample Memory
units.text: Allows a discarded branch to become relevant again upon new evidence/dependency/runtime/failure/architecture change, while storing counterexamples so universalized patterns don't become superstition.

units.name: Funnel Authority Levels
units.text: A confidence ladder (SEED, SUPPORTED, REPEATED, TRANSFERRED, PREDICTIVE, MATURE) for a branch depending on how many incidents/domains support it; used by UBC to weight it.

units.name: Funnel benchmarks (Hidden-Bug Evaluation Corpus, Unknown-Unknown Benchmarks, Funnel Mutation Testing, Governance Mutation Testing)
units.text: A family of empirical tests for RCFC itself: hiding historical root causes/fixes and measuring what branches it generates; introducing defects outside the known taxonomy; mutating context/manifestation to test for overfitting; and running the same mission under different governance rules to measure coverage/precision/TTPE/owner burden.
entities: Funnel benchmarks (Hidden-Bug Evaluation Corpus, Unknown-Unknown Benchmarks, Funnel Mutation Testing, Governance Mutation Testing)
units.canonical_key: funnel benchmarks hidden bug evaluation corpus unknown unknown benchmarks funnel mutation testing governance mutation testing

units.name: Funnel Self-Red-Team / Blind-Domain Detector / Funnel Coverage Graph
units.text: An adversary that examines the search space itself (not the product) for omitted dimensions; a detector comparing architectural surfaces against funnel attention to find blind domains (e.g., migration, accessibility, shutdown, hardware rarely investigated); and a coverage graph mapping architectural surfaces to investigated risk dimensions to tests/evidence.
entities: Funnel Self-Red-Team / Blind-Domain Detector / Funnel Coverage Graph
units.canonical_key: funnel self red team blind domain detector funnel coverage graph

units.name: Funnel Debt / Funnel Escape Incident / Funnel Recurrence Escalation
units.text: Funnel Debt registers an important branch that could not be economically resolved (scope, risk, revisit trigger — never silently PASS). A Funnel Escape Incident is logged when an owner finds a defect whose relevant branch should have activated. Recurrence of the same branch family escalates to Institutional Funnel Failure, then Compiler Integrity Incident.
entities: Funnel Debt / Funnel Escape Incident / Funnel Recurrence Escalation
units.canonical_key: funnel debt funnel escape incident funnel recurrence escalation

units.name: Long Session Memory Stack
units.text: A generalized replacement for a single STATUS.md, comprising Mission Ledger, Architecture State, Experiment Ledger, Negative Hypothesis Memory, Benchmark Frontier, Runtime Evidence, Owner Decisions, and Next Best Actions.

units.name: Game Development Session Compiler
units.text: Decides, before a large mission, among Short Execution, Focused Session, Long Autonomous Session, or Persistent Campaign, so Fable 5 isn't dispatched onto a 10-minute task nor a small session is forced into an architectural pass.

units.name: Persistent Campaign
units.text: The correct unit for building large games — not "one giant session" but a durable structure carrying Game Constitution, Production Baseline, Capability Graph, Evaluation Genome, Reference Corpus, Bug/Failure Corpus, Performance/Hardware Frontier, Build Lineage, Session Memory, and Current Milestones, allowing an executor to enter/exit without losing maturity.

units.name: Game Quality Constitution
units.text: A non-implementation-plan document per game (analogous to LAAS's PROJECT_LAAS_v2.md) containing Vision, Reference Bar, Hard Floors, Banned Outcomes, Platform Reality, and Production Definition, preventing Claude from silently lowering the target when it gets difficult.

units.name: Reference Corpus / Game Delta Intelligence
units.text: For complex games, a reference corpus (visuals, mechanics, feel, UX, architecture, performance, platform precedents) is built first; each milestone asks what still separates output from target across visual quality, movement feel, world coherence, UI, responsiveness, audio, performance, density, composition, readability.

units.name: Game Instrumentation Factory
units.text: Automatically fabricates per-campaign tooling (frame capture, input replay, deterministic playback, state inspector, collision visualizer, AI debug overlays, event timeline, save-state inspector, resource/memory profiler, scene transition tracer, hardware telemetry) as product infrastructure rather than an afterthought.

units.name: Human perception → machine evaluation ratchet
units.text: The pattern of converting a subjective human judgment ("this movement feels wrong") into a captured trace, isolated cause, and metric/probe so the machine catches it automatically next time — HIC-OAR applied to game feel.

units.name: Every Difficult Feature Pays Infrastructure Tax
units.text: A rule stating that if a feature required expensive novel investigation, the team must extract what would make the next feature of that class cheaper — producing a compounding cost curve (e.g., 20 boots → 8 → 2).
entities: Every Difficult Feature Pays Infrastructure Tax
units.canonical_key: every difficult feature pays infrastructure tax

units.name: Game Development Capability Graph
units.text: Organizes game work by capability (Boot, Input, Movement, Camera, Scene, Save, Rendering, Streaming, Audio, Physics, AI, UI, Networking, Content, Build, Deployment, Diagnostics, Recovery) each with maturity, benchmarks, known bugs, authority, and certified primitives, rather than by file.

units.name: Game Genome
units.text: Per-game-family baseline overlays (Motion Sports Game, Open World, Party Game, etc.) specifying which capabilities matter most for that family.

units.name: Self-Evolving Game Benchmarks
units.text: KMEIP applied to game capabilities — each capability benchmark escalates versions (e.g., Movement v1 "jump works" → v5 "adversarial traversal") as it saturates, retiring old versions to a Regression Vault rather than deleting them.

units.name: Fable-style API Verification
units.text: A rule (from LAAS's THREE-NOTES.md) requiring verification against the actually-installed API implementation/types before building engine architecture on model memory of an API.

units.name: Engine Knowledge Pack
units.text: Version-and-environment-bound verified knowledge about a specific engine/library (e.g., Unreal version-specific, libogc, GX), each entry with engine/version/environment/evidence fields, distinct from generic "Claude knows Unreal."

units.name: Session Rehydration Benchmark / Context Loss Mutation Tests / Stale Session Memory Detector
units.text: A benchmark giving Fable a campaign with zero chat history but durable project memory to test whether it correctly resumes; deliberate context-compaction/restart tests to verify campaign continuity; and a detector that blocks rehydration if STATUS state (e.g., a stated build) is stale relative to the actual repo.
entities: Session Rehydration Benchmark / Context Loss Mutation Tests / Stale Session Memory Detector
units.canonical_key: session rehydration benchmark context loss mutation tests stale session memory detector

units.name: Long sessions anti-drift (Milestone Rebaseline, Periodic Fresh-Eyes Agent)
units.text: Guards against drift in long campaigns by recompiling the Mission Constitution against current state at each milestone, and periodically injecting an independent fresh-eyes reviewer (low-normalization) to attack architecture/quality gaps/blind assumptions without replacing the executor.
entities: Long sessions anti-drift (Milestone Rebaseline, Periodic Fresh-Eyes Agent)
units.canonical_key: long sessions anti drift milestone rebaseline periodic fresh eyes agent

units.name: Production Game Benchmark Portfolio
units.text: A Pareto front (not a single score) across fun/feel, correctness, visual quality, performance, memory, load times, robustness, compatibility, determinism, accessibility, maintainability, production reality, where an improvement that destroys another critical dimension is not counted as improvement.

units.name: Game Production Inheritance Ratio (GPIR)
units.text: The percentage of a new game's required production maturity that is already covered before starting, distinguished from code-reuse percentage.

units.name: Human Creative Concentration (HCC)
units.text: The percentage of human intervention spent on creative direction/gameplay/feel/vision versus mechanical QA/debugging; target is creative up, mechanical toward zero.

units.name: Long-Horizon Autonomy Yield (LHAY)
units.text: How much high-quality production progress an autonomous campaign produces before needing human intervention, adjusted for regressions/rework/quality.

units.name: Plateau Detector / Representation Revolution Detector
units.text: Detects when successive iterations yield diminishing returns (e.g., 95% → 95.3% → 95.31%) and triggers a review of whether the underlying representation/architecture has a ceiling, rather than continuing microtweaks.

units.name: Generator / Evaluator / Adversary triad
units.text: A strict role separation where the Generator (Fable/Claude) builds, the Evaluator measures against target, and the Adversary actively searches for ways the result is "green but wrong" — applied here to 1:1 map/world reconstruction.

units.name: Anti-loop detector / Best-known candidate preservation / Candidate Tournament
units.text: Detects oscillating (A→B→A→B) or regressing iteration and escalates abstraction; preserves the best verified build and reverts if a new iteration is worse; runs competing strategies as challengers benchmarked against each other rather than sequential blind insistence.
entities: Anti-loop detector / Best-known candidate preservation / Candidate Tournament
units.canonical_key: anti loop detector best known candidate preservation candidate tournament

units.name: Hierarchical convergence ordering (Macro→Micro)
units.text: Orders reconstruction work Macro Geometry → Spatial Layout → Meso Detail → Materials → Lighting → Micro Detail, since fixing micro detail is wasted if macro geometry is wrong; KIFS/IFC decides which mismatch has the greatest perceptual contribution.

units.name: Universal Reference Convergence Engine
units.text: A generalized capability applying reference→evaluator→delta→iterate→convergence to any domain (visual, behavioral, API, CLI, game world, protocol, data transformation), not just 3D worlds — e.g., "clone this API 1:1" or "migrate with zero behavior delta."

units.name: Premature Stop Rate (PSR) / User "Continue" Rate (UCR) / First-Intent Completion Rate (FICR)
units.text: PSR counts autonomously-resolvable tasks Claude incorrectly returned incomplete (target 0). UCR counts how often the user must say "continue"/"keep going" (target 0 for non-irreducibly-human tasks). FICR measures the percentage of missions reaching Production Reality with a single initial user intervention.
entities: Premature Stop Rate (PSR) / User "Continue" Rate (UCR) / First-Intent Completion Rate (FICR)
units.canonical_key: premature stop rate psr user continue rate ucr first intent completion rate ficr

units.name: Contract Convergence vs Frontier Evolution
units.text: Distinguishes satisfying what the user actually requested (Contract Convergence, which permits declaring Done) from ongoing self-improvement research after completion (Frontier Evolution), which must not be conflated.

units.name: Universal Constrained Reimplementation & Semantic Portability Capability
units.text: A generalized capability (derived from analyzing CavEX, a from-scratch Wii-native Minecraft Beta reimplementation) for reconstructing a system's essential capabilities under radically different platform constraints by preserving semantics while completely replacing representation, rather than translating source code line-by-line.
entities: Universal Constrained Reimplementation & Semantic Portability Capability
units.canonical_key: universal constrained reimplementation semantic portability capability

units.name: Target Satisfaction Contract
units.text: A compiled, verifiable set of claims (Geometry, Spatial, Material, Lighting, Camera, Visual, Runtime Fidelity) that operationalizes what "1:1" or "100%" means for a given reconstruction task, replacing subjective interpretation.

units.name: Constraint Genome
units.text: A per-platform enumeration of hard resource/environment constraints (CPU, MEM1/MEM2, GX, EFB, storage, controller, video modes for Wii; DOM/WebGPU/memory/sandbox for browser; kilobytes RAM/no-OS/power for microcontroller) used to ask what architecture turns constraints into a design advantage rather than an endless patch series.

units.name: Reference Reconstruction Pipeline
units.text: The Fable/LAAS-derived loop: reference acquisition → ground-truth extraction → semantic decomposition → scene reconstruction → render → reference comparison → delta map → rank mismatches → correct → re-render → repeat.

units.name: Viewpoint Overfitting detector
units.text: Generates multiple views (original, orthographic-ish, opposite side, top, traversal, close-ups) to detect a reconstruction that looks perfect from one camera but is wrong elsewhere ("Viewpoint Overfitting").

units.name: Capability Budget Compiler
units.text: Assigns CPU/memory/GPU/I/O/latency/storage budgets to each desired capability against a global budget before implementation, so Claude doesn't discover "it doesn't fit" only at the end.

units.name: Geometry Comparator / Visual Comparator / Semantic Comparator / Perceptual Delta Heatmap
units.text: A suite of differential evaluators: structural geometry comparison (missing/extra volumes, wrong scale/topology), multi-dimension visual comparison (silhouette, composition, color, lighting, texture, vegetation, landmark, depth, atmosphere) rather than a single score, semantic comparison of landmark roles/hierarchy, and a per-pixel heatmap directing iteration to the largest deviations.
entities: Geometry Comparator / Visual Comparator / Semantic Comparator / Perceptual Delta Heatmap
units.canonical_key: geometry comparator visual comparator semantic comparator perceptual delta heatmap

units.name: Representation Search
units.text: Instead of only asking "how do I optimize this," asks whether an entirely different, orders-of-magnitude-cheaper representation of the problem exists (e.g., individual blocks → chunk mesh/display lists, as in CavEX).

units.name: PATCH/ADAPT/REIMPLEMENT/EMULATE/SUBSTITUTE/HYBRID decision compiler
units.text: A per-subsystem architectural decision compiler choosing among six strategies (modify existing retail implementation, reuse behind an adapter, recreate semantics independently, maintain compatibility behavior, use a simpler equivalent, or combine original+native) based on evidence rather than a fixed doctrine ("always fork" or "always rewrite").
units.canonical_key: patch adapt reimplement emulate substitute hybrid decision compiler

units.name: Closed Composition
units.text: Requires that every existing element (artifact, service, dependency, scheduled job, database, process, route) be able to justify its membership (what it is, who created/owns/consumes it, its lifecycle, why it's still legitimate), rather than "it can stay as long as it doesn't bother anyone."

units.name: Failure Generation Grammar
units.text: A generative mechanism producing new failure hypotheses by combining dimensions (Object × Lifecycle × Scope × Authority × State × Transition × Concurrency × Failure Mode × Observability × Consequence), turning a static Failure Library into a Failure Generator.

units.name: Interaction Pair/Triple Mining (risk-guided)
units.text: Searches the Capability Graph for pairs/triples of individually-correct capabilities that jointly produce invalid global state, using risk-guided search rather than full cartesian testing.
units.canonical_key: interaction pair triple mining risk guided

units.name: Human Infrastructure Dependency
units.text: Treats any correctness-critical human memory ("remember to restart twice," "don't delete that folder") as undeclared infrastructure requiring documentation → automation → enforcement → elimination.

units.name: Correctness Laundering / Manifest Laundering Detection
units.text: Forbids changing expected state to make reality appear passing (updating an allowlist when garbage appears, marking a missing feature optional, marking a broken journey out of scope, lowering a benchmark threshold) unless intent/evidence genuinely changed.

units.name: Anti-Goodhart Engineering
units.text: Explicitly catalogs and guards against gaming of institutional metrics themselves (one-shot gaming, root cleanliness gaming, test-count gaming, flywheel deposit gaming); "reusable asset created" only counts as learning if future applicable work actually benefited.

units.name: Negative Transfer Detection
units.text: Measures REUSE OUTCOME rather than assuming reuse is inherently valuable, since a lesson that helps one system can harm another; protects UBC from becoming overly aggressive.

units.name: Capability Reality Level ladder (Exists→Production-Proven)
units.text: A nine-step maturity ladder (Exists → Wired → Exercisable → Player/User-visible → Persistent → Recoverable → Operable → Evolvable → Production-Proven) superseding "code exists" or "tests green" as the definition of Done, preventing phantom completeness.
units.canonical_key: capability reality level ladder exists production proven

units.name: Factory Capital / Reconstructability Capital / Surprise Capital
units.text: New institutional capital types: Factory Capital (persistent capacity to produce a system class with less uncertainty/intervention/surprise), Reconstructability Capital (how much of a system can be destroyed and faithfully regenerated), Surprise Capital (acquired capacity to anticipate previously unknown surprise classes).
entities: Factory Capital / Reconstructability Capital / Surprise Capital
units.canonical_key: factory capital reconstructability capital surprise capital

units.name: Engineering Reality Encoder / Universal Semantic IR
units.text: A perception layer (analogous to a model's perception encoder) that ingests source, ASTs, binaries, diffs, logs, stack traces, screenshots, UI, video frames, tests, profiling, DB, filesystem, network topology, processes, hardware telemetry, deployments, CI, operator actions, and transforms them into canonical entities (Artifact, Capability, Owner, Dependency, State, Transition, Invariant, Boundary, Side Effect, Failure, Evidence, Claim, Experiment, Environment, Consumer, Provider, Human Intervention, Benchmark, Production Effect).
entities: Engineering Reality Encoder / Universal Semantic IR
units.canonical_key: engineering reality encoder universal semantic ir

units.name: Engineering Attention Intelligence (context locality tiers)
units.text: Models UBC as an "engineering attention mechanism" with local (files touched, immediate dependencies), architectural (module/system), estate (deployment/runtime), and global institutional (universal capabilities/failures/baselines) attention tiers, so not every mission loads all 40 datasets.
units.canonical_key: engineering attention intelligence context locality tiers

units.name: Durable Context Architecture / Effective Engineering Memory
units.text: Rejects "give Claude more context window" in favor of externalized durable memory (Mission Ledger, Construction DNA, Knowledge Vault, Architecture State, Experiment Ledger, Failure Ledger, Decision Ledger, Production Estate, Campaign State) so Fable can lose context and keep working.
entities: Durable Context Architecture / Effective Engineering Memory
units.canonical_key: durable context architecture effective engineering memory

units.name: Three definitions of one-shot (Human One-Shot, Factory First-Pass, Novelty One-Shot)
units.text: Distinguishes a single human intention with autonomous iteration (Human One-Shot), the first produced artifact passing all gates (Factory First-Pass), and sustained performance under sufficiently novel composition (Novelty One-Shot) — since memorizing 20 prior setups doesn't prove general engineering.
entities: Three definitions of one-shot (Human One-Shot, Factory First-Pass, Novelty One-Shot)
units.canonical_key: three definitions of one shot human one shot factory first pass novelty one shot

units.name: One-Shot Distance
units.text: A vector distance to production comprising Architecture Gap, Composition Gap, Integration Gap, Runtime Gap, User Journey Gap, Reliability Gap, Operational Gap, Production Reality Gap, Human Intervention Gap — observable evidence of whether CPP is actually improving.

units.name: Speculative Engineering / Engineering Draft Engine
units.text: Modeled on speculative decoding — a cheap agent proposes candidates (architecture, likely fix, test set, capability mapping) which a stronger executor/verifier validates, rather than running everything through the most expensive cognitive resource.

units.name: Minimum Surprise Engineering / Production Surprise Rate
units.text: Classifies surprises (Construction, Boot, Integration, Player, Operations, Production, Evolution Surprise) and measures whether each generation contains fewer important things the factory failed to anticipate, aiming to move from trial-and-error to predictive engineering.
entities: Minimum Surprise Engineering / Production Surprise Rate
units.canonical_key: minimum surprise engineering production surprise rate

units.name: Institutional Knowledge Compression (quantization analogy) / Compression degradation measurement
units.text: Models UKDL compression on model quantization — Full Evidence → rich Knowledge Vault → compressed causal knowledge → Mission Capsule — and proposes measuring whether a compressed pack still anticipates bugs/selects architecture/detects failure as well as full evidence.
entities: Institutional Knowledge Compression (quantization analogy) / Compression degradation measurement
units.canonical_key: institutional knowledge compression quantization analogy compression degradation measurement

units.name: Preventable Escape Depth / Maturity ladder (L0-L4)
units.text: For each failure, asks at what earlier point it could have been prevented (production→runtime sentinel→postdeploy→predeploy→integration test→construction validator→compiler→primitive→structurally impossible), formalized as a five-level maturity ladder L0 DISCOVERABLE→L4 STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE.
units.canonical_key: preventable escape depth maturity ladder l0 l4

units.name: Deployment envelope variants (Full/Runtime/CI/Portable/Edge/Domain Baseline)
units.text: Multiple packaging forms of the same institutional intelligence for different consumption contexts (Full Institutional Baseline, Runtime Baseline for Claude Code, CI Baseline for deterministic gates, Portable Baseline for non-CPP projects, Edge Baseline for small repos, Domain Packs for Wii/Game/Web).
units.canonical_key: deployment envelope variants full runtime ci portable edge domain baseline

units.name: Cold Birth / Estate-Wide Cold Birth
units.text: Requires that a system be constructible entirely from declared source, dependencies, configuration, and data/bootstrap without mysterious historical state, manual operator steps, or hidden secrets; extended to the whole estate since individual components can each cold-birth correctly while the network as a whole fails due to hidden startup-ordering dependencies.
units.canonical_key: cold birth estate wide cold birth

units.name: Engineering Baseline Card
units.text: A model-card-style document per baseline covering Overview, Capability Coverage, Architecture, Applicable Domains, Benchmarks, Known Limitations, Failure Modes, Safety/Operational Constraints, Deployment Forms, Provenance.

units.name: Reconstructability
units.text: The master proof of maturity: whether, if the current instance were destroyed, the same correct product could be reconstructed from declared sources without depending on history, hotfixes, human memory, or residue.

units.name: Six realities convergence model
units.text: A six-state model of a system (Intended, Constructed, Deployed, Running, Experienced, Reconstructable) that must all converge, forming a richer definition of Production Reality.

units.name: Convergence Engineering / Stable Convergence
units.text: Requires that after boot, operation, restart, and background generation, the system reaches a known stable state; flags failure modes where restart creates a new file, changes IDs, rewrites config, or two components eternally "correct" each other.

units.name: Factory/Runtime mismatch detection
units.text: Detects cases where the factory's model of the system (config immutable, single-process, cold-start, manifest authoritative) diverges from actual runtime behavior (mutated config, wrapper process, persistent volume, separate generated registry).

units.name: Universal Engineering Benchmark Suite
units.text: A multi-category benchmark portfolio (Construction, Production Reality, Failure Anticipation, Reconstructability, Long-Horizon, Hidden Failure, Cross-Domain Transfer, Novelty benchmarks) measuring whether the engineering civilization actually works, mirroring Muse Glimmer's evaluation categories.

units.name: Effective State / Production Artifact Identity
units.text: Distinguishes declared/config-file state from effective/running state (config file ≠ effective config, manifest ≠ production, artifact on disk ≠ artifact running); demands stable identity/role/owner/provenance rather than identifying things by mutable name/path/version string/label.

units.name: Institutional Pretraining / Post-Training analogy
units.text: Models broad external engineering history (repos, bugs, papers, production systems) as "institutional pretraining" producing broad priors, and CPP's own reality (owner corrections, actual incidents, hardware) as "post-training" producing alignment with how the institution wants to build.

units.name: Outcome-Conditioned Institutional Learning
units.text: An RL-inspired mechanism where an architecture's authority rises or falls based on measured outcomes (iterations, escapes) rather than expert opinion alone.

units.name: Irreversible Action Model
units.text: Classifies actions as REVERSIBLE, RECOVERABLE, COMPENSATABLE, or IRREVERSIBLE; UBC compiles required evidence/approval/rollback per class, connecting to KSEIP's destructive-operations doctrine.

units.name: Engineering Capability Vector / Engineering Capability Frontier
units.text: An explicit live map of institutional capacities across dimensions (Persistence, Recovery, Migration, Rendering, Distributed state, Reverse engineering, Wii, Game development, etc.) with a moving frontier — when a capability matures it moves to the Regression Vault and the frontier advances to a harder problem (KMEIP applied to the institution itself).
entities: Engineering Capability Vector / Engineering Capability Frontier
units.canonical_key: engineering capability vector engineering capability frontier

units.name: Baseline release engineering (Challenger baselines)
units.text: Treats the baseline itself as a production product: Baseline Candidate → historical replay → hidden eval → canary projects → comparative benchmark → Pareto Gate → promotion; a new version is only promoted if it beats the prior on the same corpus (fewer false activations, less TTPE, more quality).

units.name: Self-evolving training loop (UEFB flywheel)
units.text: The full cycle: real software work → telemetry/discoveries → Evidence Store → Construction DNA → failure/success analysis → RCFC → causal abstractions → new candidates → hidden/historical evaluation → baseline challenger → canary → promotion → UBC learns routing → future mission → outcome attribution → next generation.
units.canonical_key: self evolving training loop uefb flywheel

units.name: Self-play engineering / Synthetic Failure Curriculum
units.text: A Generator/Adversary/Evaluator/Repair loop that synthetically generates engineering experience (artificial lifecycle bugs, stale state, version skew, interaction triples via the Failure Generation Grammar) to test whether agents/tests anticipate them, accelerating maturity without waiting for production incidents.
units.canonical_key: self play engineering synthetic failure curriculum

units.name: Universal External Reality Acquisition & Evolution Layer
units.text: A universal layer converting the public web and other navigable external surfaces into versioned, reproducible, semantically structured, continuously updatable evidence for the entire Engineering Foundation Runtime, with Scrapling (a web scraping/crawling tool) as one principal adapter rather than the whole architecture.
entities: Universal External Reality Acquisition & Evolution Layer
units.canonical_key: universal external reality acquisition evolution layer

units.name: Source Authority Router
units.text: Before acquiring information, determines the best available source in priority order (installed implementation/types → official docs → upstream repo → changelog → issues → secondary sources); Scrapling is only the acquisition mechanism, never the authority decider.

units.name: Documentation Reality Workflow
units.text: The pipeline for acquiring library/framework knowledge: crawl official docs → convert to clean Markdown/structured records → version-lock → extract APIs/constraints/deprecations → compare with installed package → detect contradictions → produce Mission Knowledge Pack.

units.name: Documentation Drift Intelligence / External Knowledge Drift Intelligence
units.text: When an adaptive web parser relocates an extraction target after a site's structure changes, a Source Drift Event is created and verified (same concept? DOM-only change? semantic change? version change?) rather than silently trusting relocation.
entities: Documentation Drift Intelligence / External Knowledge Drift Intelligence
units.canonical_key: documentation drift intelligence external knowledge drift intelligence

units.name: Adaptive Extraction Confidence
units.text: Per-field confidence classification (EXACT_MATCH, STRUCTURALLY_RELOCATED, SEMANTICALLY_VALIDATED, AMBIGUOUS, BROKEN, REMOVED) so "scraper still works" does not imply "knowledge is still correct."

units.name: Persistent Research Campaigns / Research Development Replay
units.text: Uses Scrapling's checkpoint/resume and dev-mode response caching to make large research crawls (e.g., 20,000 pages) durable and interruptible, and to let successive parser/extractor/analyzer versions replay against the same captured evidence deterministically.
entities: Persistent Research Campaigns / Research Development Replay
units.canonical_key: persistent research campaigns research development replay

units.name: External Failure Corpus Mining / External Contradiction Hunting
units.text: Mines bug reports, release regressions, migration failures, compatibility problems from external mature software to feed UFIA's Failure Genome pipeline; also hunts contradictions between what docs/vendors claim and what runtime/issue-trackers actually show.
entities: External Failure Corpus Mining / External Contradiction Hunting
units.canonical_key: external failure corpus mining external contradiction hunting

units.name: Evidence Firewall / Untrusted Evidence Quarantine
units.text: A mandatory pipeline (raw web content → sanitizer → injection detector → semantic extraction → claim isolation → source authority classification → evidence graph) ensuring raw external content never becomes an agent instruction stream, treating all external content as untrusted data even after Scrapling's own sanitization.

units.name: Acquisition Router (Tier 0-4)
units.text: Routes acquisition requests through cost tiers (Tier 0 existing cache, Tier 1 static HTTP, Tier 2 structured feeds/API, Tier 3 dynamic browser, Tier 4 authenticated/remote environment), avoiding heavy browser launches for static pages; IFC optimizes cost.

units.name: Software Evolution Intelligence (external acquisition integration)
units.text: A pre-existing system for discovering external software patterns/architectures/capabilities, which uses UERAL as its acquisition plane (mining repos, docs, release notes, blogs, benchmarks, compatibility data, issues) and decides what's worth incorporating, including External Capability Discovery (detecting when an external library supersedes a custom CPP primitive).
units.canonical_key: software evolution intelligence external acquisition integration

units.name: External Reality Coverage (ERC)
units.text: The percentage of external assumptions relevant to a mission that are backed by current attributable evidence.

units.name: Source Freshness Debt (SFD)
units.text: How much active knowledge depends on evidence older than its allowed freshness window.

units.name: Crawl Failure Genomes
units.text: A generalization of UFIA's Failure Genome pattern to crawling: five named failure modes (e.g. HTTP-200-but-error-page "succeeding," crawler queue empty but hidden pagination missed, adaptive selector relocating without semantic check, multiple pages citing the same upstream read as independent, session-authenticated content stored as universal).

units.name: External Assumption Registry
units.text: A registry for architectural assumptions that depend on external facts ("API supports X", "library requires Y"), each carrying source, version, evidence, freshness, consumers and a revalidation policy.

units.name: Capability Challenger System
units.text: Launches a challenger evaluation when Crawl OS discovers an upstream implementation that is faster, more reliable or cheaper than an internal one, rather than keeping the internal implementation simply because it exists.

units.name: Crawl Construction DNA
units.text: A per-campaign record of mission, strategies, engines, source types, frontier, pages, failures, retries, selector repairs, cost, latency, evidence yield, claims supported and human intervention.

units.name: Evidence Replay Runtime
units.text: A certified primitive, inspired by Scrapling's development cache, that lets any stored external response feed new parsers/extractors/analyzers without re-hitting the original source, increasing determinism and reducing traffic/cost.

units.name: Structural Loss Detector
units.text: A new detector that flags what disappeared during normalization (table relationships, footnotes, captions, charts, images, layout semantics) and escalates to multimodal inspection when the loss is material.

units.name: Authenticated Research Vault
units.text: An existing Crawl OS concept extended with identity-specific scope, allowed domains, expiry, purpose limitation and audit trail so authenticated-session evidence cannot automatically become universal public knowledge.

units.name: Public/Private Knowledge Boundary
units.text: A classification scheme (PUBLIC / INTERNAL / PROJECT-CONFIDENTIAL / CUSTOMER-RESTRICTED) that universalization of evidence must respect rather than moving anything technically reusable into a global corpus.

units.name: Production Reality Gates (K–O extension)
units.text: Five new gates added to the existing ten Production Reality Gates, checking source authority sufficiency, semantic identity of extracted concepts, real evidence independence, institutional scope safety, and propagation of impact when evidence changes.
units.canonical_key: production reality gates k o extension

units.name: Knowledge Compilation Pipeline
units.text: A pipeline turning an Evidence Package into Structural Map → Concepts → Mental Models → Decision Rules → Patterns → Anti-patterns → Trade-offs → Failure Conditions → Applicability → Counterexamples → Operational Actions → Projection, going beyond mere summarization to actual decision-changing capability.

units.name: Knowledge Skill Intermediate Representation
units.text: A model-independent intermediate form (Identity, Purpose, Triggers, Negative Triggers, Applicable/Non-Applicable Contexts, Mental Models, Decision Rules, Patterns, Anti-Patterns, Procedures, Failure Modes, Evidence References, Confidence, Topics, Retrieval Units, Required Tools, Expected Outputs, Evals, Lifecycle) compiled before any concrete SKILL.md, enabling projection to Claude/Copilot/Amp/future formats.

units.name: Knowledge Rediscovery Tax
units.text: The universalized cost (tokens, tool calls, reads, searches, time) spent reconstructing knowledge CPP already acquired, generalized from book-to-skill's "Discovery Loop Tax" for repeatedly re-navigating the same document.

units.name: Skill Quality Gate
units.text: A ten-part gate ladder (structural validity, topic discoverability, claim traceability, positive+negative triggers, decision-changing utility, non-lossy compression, injection/security safety, regression retention, context-cost efficiency, cross-domain non-contamination) stronger than book-to-skill's per-host validator.

units.name: Skill Poisoning benchmark
units.text: An adversarial corpus (normal book, hidden Unicode instruction, fake system prompt, malicious appendix, authority-widening instruction, data exfiltration request) checking that source text never grants a generated skill extra authority.
units.parent: Universal Evaluation Fabric / Skill Quality Gate

units.name: Skill Consumer Telemetry
units.text: Per-skill tracking of applicable missions, activated missions, files/topics loaded, tokens, decisions changed, errors prevented, false activations and missed activations.

units.name: Skill Reachability
units.text: Detects "dead" skills that exist but never activate (an AISHF-recognized failure class), and a benchmark measuring activation precision/recall/false-activation/missed-activation against a mission corpus.

units.name: Capability Fitness Arena
units.text: A comparison arena for competing skills covering the same work class, measured on outcome, TTPE, tokens, errors, human intervention, with the winner becoming authority instead of maintaining five equivalent skills.

units.name: Skill Lifecycle
units.text: A nine-state lifecycle: CANDIDATE → GENERATED → VALIDATED → SHADOW → ACTIVE → MATURE → SUPERSEDED → DEPRECATED → RETIRED, ensuring "no eternal skills."

units.name: Self-evolving Skill Compiler
units.text: A compiler that reports what was used, never loaded, missed queries, raw-source reopens and wrong decisions per compilation, and uses that to improve its own indexing, granularity, trigger descriptions and compression.

units.name: Exactness Ladder
units.text: A tiered fidelity contract (Structural / Behaviorally / Numerically / Byte / Perceptually / User-Outcome / Production Equivalent) so a test result states WHAT KIND of equivalence was proven, not just PASS.

units.name: Fixture Genome
units.text: Treats test fixtures as versioned engineering assets, each declaring which defect family it kills, which plausible-wrong implementation it discriminates, its boundary, tolerance, producing oracle and version.

units.name: Mission Environment Doctor
units.text: A universalization of kimi-k3-in-c's k3-doctor.sh: checks toolchain/memory/storage/environment before an expensive build/run and recommends the viable execution mode/preset.

units.name: Constraint Envelope Compilation
units.text: Compiles per-family minimum/recommended/high-performance/degraded resource envelopes together with semantic invariants, applicable from Wii to 8GB laptops to huge servers.

units.name: Repository Completeness Pack
units.text: A logical (not necessarily file-per-file) set of README/QUICKSTART/ARCHITECTURE/CONFIGURATION/API/TESTING/BENCHMARKING/PERFORMANCE/TUNING/RECOVERY/SECURITY/OPERATIONS/COMPATIBILITY/ROADMAP/RAW EVIDENCE/CHANGELOG artifacts compiled per project by UBC/UPSEIP.

units.name: Certified Capability Package
units.text: An elevated definition of "certified primitive" bundling Implementation, Contract, Tiny Oracle, Adversarial Fixtures, Regression Genome, Benchmark, Resource Envelope, Diagnostics, Evidence, Compatibility and Known Limitations — not implementation alone.
units.parent: Baseline Completeness Genome / Constitutive Baseline Ratchet

units.name: Runtime & Surface Completeness
units.text: A new Completeness Genome column contributed by analyzing OpenCode: maturity is defined not only by core logic but by how a system is consumed by humans/programs, executor-switched, context-maintained, tool-authorized, extended, and exposed across UI/CLI/API behind one semantic authority.

units.name: Context Epochs
units.text: Generalized from OpenCode V2's structured session-context snapshotting: context (baseline generation, Project Genome, skills, rules, environment facts, model, tool capabilities, permissions) is versioned runtime state, and any change produces a new epoch/delta rather than an invisible mutation.

units.name: Scoped Capability Overlay
units.text: A layering primitive (Global baseline → Domain override → Project override → Mission experimental override) with automatic reversion to parent authority when a mission ends, each override carrying lineage (parent capability, override, scope, reason, evidence, expiry).

units.name: Machine Operability
units.text: A new Completeness Genome dimension distinguishing Human Operability, Machine Operability (can automation/agents operate it via stable contracts?), and Parity between them.

units.name: Universal Execution Identity
units.text: A causal-lineage identity tuple (institutional mission, project, workspace/worktree, session, agent, model/provider, baseline generation, artifact generation) drawn from OpenCode's project/workspace/session separation.

units.name: Context Source Registry
units.text: A registry of context sources (CLAUDE.md, UKDL, Knowledge Runtime, Skill Projection, UBC) with precedence, scope, freshness and epoch reconciliation, extracted from OpenCode's AGENTS.md/rules hierarchy without duplicating the existing rules system.

units.name: Knowledge CAS
units.text: Every material institutional write must know its parent generation, expected version and produce a new generation or detect conflicts, preventing "last writer silently wins" — especially once Agent Teams write in parallel.

units.name: Institutional Lost Update
units.text: A new UFIA failure family where one agent, writing from a stale snapshot, silently erases a doctrine/knowledge correction another agent had already added (e.g. re-adding "Primitive X is unsafe on Windows" after it was removed) — the institution "unlearns" without the software failing yet.

units.name: Semantic Identity Registry
units.text: Extends the Capability Authority Registry with canonical identity, aliases, former names, semantic fingerprints and supersession lineage, so "Durable Session Continuity" and "Persistent Campaign Recovery" don't become two infrastructures for one capability.

units.name: Institutional Retraction Propagation
units.text: When invalidated evidence (E1) supported a hypothesis→capability→baseline chain, deletion must propagate through the Dependency Lineage rather than only marking E1, reaching every derivative before it's considered handled.

units.name: Source-vs-Projection Semantics
units.text: Classifies every knowledge representation as Authority / Projection / Cache / Index / Summary / Derived View (e.g. raw benchmark output = Authority; performance report = Projection; agent context capsule = Cache), so a convenience layer never accidentally becomes the primary database.

units.name: Relevance-Gated Knowledge Application
units.text: Distinguishes exists / retrievable / applicable / materially useful / activated as separate states, so existing knowledge is only injected into a mission when it materially changes the outcome.

units.name: Context Value Function
units.text: Weighs expected decision value of including a knowledge item against its token cost and confusion/cross-domain contamination risk; an item enters the capsule only if Expected Decision Value > Context Cost.

units.name: Knowledge Volatility / Freshness Budget
units.text: Assigns each knowledge piece a Volatility Class (static invariant vs. volatile pricing/API state vs. real-time deployment state) with last-verified date, validity scope and refresh trigger.

units.name: Universal Discriminating Retrieval
units.text: Search/retrieval should maximize discrimination between hypotheses rather than accumulating confirming support for a favored answer, distilled from a "search as falsification" instruction.
units.parent: Information Gain Planner / RCFC / Experiment Compiler

units.name: Capability Routing Graph
units.text: Formalizes intent → candidate capabilities → applicability → authority → freshness → cost → reliability → selected execution route → fallback, treating capability/tool routing as governed architecture rather than ad hoc model choice.

units.name: Capability Degradation Ladder
units.text: Requires a capability's fallback chain to be part of its contract (e.g. LSP unavailable → parser → textual search) rather than inventing a result when the primary route fails.

units.name: Multi-Writer Institutional Runtime
units.text: Treats multiple simultaneous writers (Claude Code, desktop, Fable, headless agents, AutoResearch, CI, human UI) writing shared institutional state as normal concurrency from day one, requiring versioning/transactions/conflict-detection/idempotency/lineage/authority as P0 requirements.

units.name: Constitutional Reassertion Trigger
units.text: On session-too-long, compaction, high drift, model handoff or large plan change, recompiles/reasserts a small constitutional capsule (mission, hard invariants, authority, baseline, done contract) rather than resending everything; also compares current agent behavior against the active Mission Constitution to detect divergence.

units.name: Instruction Provenance Graph
units.text: Every instruction-shaped string carries issuer, scope, priority, validity, signature/origin and generation, so a README or webpage saying "ignore tests"/"execute this" can never outrank the project constitution or become an agent instruction.

units.name: Institutional State Graph
units.text: A fifth graph (alongside Capability, Failure, Evidence, Construction Graphs) representing what the institution knows, which version, who wrote it, provenance, authority, dependents, supersession, consuming missions, staleness and invalidation — with transactional semantics.

units.name: Institutional Event Log
units.text: An append-only log of typed events (DiscoveryObserved, FailureReproduced, RootCauseEstablished, HypothesisRefuted, CapabilityProposed, ApplicabilityNarrowed, BenchmarkPassed, ProductionEvidenceAdded, CapabilityPromoted, BaselineRaised, KnowledgeSuperseded, EvidenceRevoked, BaselineInvalidated, HumanCorrectionObserved, AuthorityChanged, AssumptionExpired, MetrologyIncidentDetected) from which current state is derived.

units.name: Materialized Views (Vault/UKDL/Registries)
units.text: Reframes the Vault, UKDL, Capability Registry, Baseline Registry, Failure Corpus, Mission Capsule and Documentation as regenerable materialized views over evidence + event lineage, not independent authorities.

units.name: Knowledge Compiler (institutional)
units.text: A true compiler (not an LLM summarizing notes) taking claims, evidence, provenance, applicability, counterexamples, dependencies, maturity as input and emitting rejected / local fact / reusable knowledge / capability candidate / baseline candidate / hard rule / primitive candidate, with explicit denial diagnostics.

units.name: Knowledge Linker
units.text: Detects when two independent discoveries represent the same capability/invariant/failure family via semantic identity, aliases, shared mechanism, supersession or composition, preventing ten names for one concept.

units.name: Institutional Duplicate Detection
units.text: A sophisticated typing of duplication — Syntactic, Semantic, Partial, Competing Authority, Temporal, Composition Duplicate — beyond mere name similarity.

units.name: Institutional Referential Cascade
units.text: Explicit foreign-key-like dependency links (Baseline→Capability→Invariant→Evidence) so revoking evidence reports exactly how many capabilities/baseline activations transitively depend on it, cascading degradation through claims → capabilities → baseline generations → missions → primitives (quarantine).

units.name: Institutional ACID Semantics
units.text: Frames important baseline promotions as transactions (BEGIN → validate identity/generation/evidence/applicability/dependencies/conflicts → compile regressions → apply state → update indexes → emit event → COMMIT, else ROLLBACK).

units.name: Institutional Consistency Model
units.text: Declares consistency requirements per state class (raw observations = append-only, experiments = causal, local project knowledge = eventual, capability maturity = strong, global baseline = serializable, authority registry = strongly consistent, context caches = rebuildable/eventual).
entities: State classes with differentiated consistency envelopes

units.name: Institutional Branches
units.text: "Git for institutional doctrine" — a risky proposal doesn't mutate the active baseline immediately; it becomes an experimental branch (e.g. Generation 53-X) tested via shadow missions, historical replay and canaries before merge or discard.

units.name: A/B Testing of Constitutions
units.text: Runs competing baseline generations (e.g. old vs Fable-derived error-handling doctrine) over the same historical construction tasks, measuring TTPE, failure rate, human interventions, regressions and token cost so doctrine evolves by evidence.

units.name: Institutional Replay Engine
units.text: Replays any new rule/capability/baseline/router/prompt/skill against historical Construction Events (and counterfactually, World-A-vs-World-B) to ask whether it would have prevented real past failures, producing Counterfactual Institutional Evidence.

units.name: Baseline Deployment Safety
units.text: New doctrine is rolled out to a small percentage (e.g. 5%) of compatible missions first, measured for improvement/false activation/cost/unexpected interaction, before expanding to 25%/100%; degrading generations are rolled back but preserved with reason/failure evidence, never silently repeated.

units.name: Bitemporal Institutional Knowledge
units.text: Separates Reality Time (when something was true in the world) from Institutional Time (when CPP learned it), plus valid_from/valid_until/observed_at/verified_at/superseded_at, so questions like "why didn't we prevent this in February?" are answerable.

units.name: Institutional Knowledge Latency
units.text: Decomposes the time from reality-change to first successful application into Discovery Latency, Institutionalization Latency, Activation Latency and Behavioral Impact Latency; TTIA is the auxiliary north-star measuring time from discovering an improvement to it actually benefiting future construction.

units.name: Institutionalization ROI
units.text: Formalizes whether a candidate learning deserves institutionalization as Expected Future Frequency × Expected Severity Avoided × Reuse Surface × Confidence × Automation Potential ÷ Institutionalization Cost.

units.name: Knowledge Debt
units.text: A quantifiable debt taxonomy parallel to technical debt: discoveries captured but uninterpreted, conflicting authorities unresolved, stale unrevalidated knowledge, un-productized known capabilities, unenforced rules, and old systems non-compliant with new standards.

units.name: Institutional Garbage Collector
units.text: Classifies knowledge as ACTIVE/COLD/OBSOLETE/SUPERSEDED/DEAD/UNUSED/WRONG using consumption telemetry (e.g. a rule never activated across 10,000 missions triggers investigation rather than infinite accumulation).

units.name: Knowledge Half-Life
units.text: Per-type decay characteristic (fundamental algorithms = huge half-life; library APIs, pricing = short) used by UBC to decide trust-cached vs. revalidate.

units.name: Engineering Policy VM
units.text: Frames the compiled Mission Capsule as executable policy run by whichever model (Claude, Fable, GPT, future model) receives it, so model capability becomes replaceable compute while the institution retains its engineering civilization.

units.name: Capability Bytecode
units.text: A structured intermediate representation of a capability (Capability ID, Preconditions, Applicability, Required Evidence, Allowed Operations, Forbidden States, Verification Oracle, Fallback, Recovery, Completion, Production Receipt) that Markdown, prompt, CI rule, agent tool and lint rule are all compiled from, preventing policy drift across six manual copies.

units.name: Knowledge → Enforcement Compiler
units.text: The full ascension chain Observation → Invariant → Doctrine → Structured Policy → Enforcement Target → Runtime Guard → Certified Primitive, with the terminal form being "impossible-by-construction" behavior.

units.name: Proof-Carrying Capabilities
units.text: A promoted capability bundling identity, implementation, tests, benchmarks, evidence, failure coverage, applicability, version and certificate, so UBC verifies a certificate rather than re-reading the whole corpus, with expiry conditions (e.g. "expires if dependency X changes major version").

units.name: Institutional Observability
units.text: The institution audits itself, not just software — asking which rules never activate, which activations produce false positives, which promotions were later reverted, which owners overlap, which evidence dependencies are fragile, which domains generate too many human corrections, which routers have low precision.

units.name: Institutional SLOs
units.text: Reliability targets for the institution's own intelligence: Material Discovery Loss <0.1%, Known-Failure Recurrence <0.5%, Stale-Authority Activation <0.1%, Baseline Inheritance >99%, Human Rediscovery <1%, Institutional Lost Updates =0, Revocation Propagation <10min, Duplicate Authority Creation <0.1%.

units.name: Institutional Incident Response
units.text: Treats a corrupted-baseline propagation as a severity-1 production incident: detect → quarantine generation → stop propagation → identify dependent missions → rollback → causal RCA → fix mechanism → replay → re-enable.

units.name: Institutional Blast Radius
units.text: Every mutation carries a predicted impact scope (1 project / 10 projects / family-wide / domain-wide / universal); required promotion confidence scales non-linearly with that scope, so a local heuristic needs a cheap gate while a constitutional rule needs an extremely high one.

units.name: Epistemic Quorum
units.text: For high-blast-radius changes, requires evidence diversity (runtime evidence, historical replay, independent evaluator, counterexample search, production canary) rather than three agents repeating the same conclusion; institutional consensus is explicitly not majority vote.

units.name: Institutional Fault Injection
units.text: Deliberately injects a stale capability card, conflicting baseline, lost update, missing knowledge, wrong alias, invalid evidence, outdated dependency, false authority or partial context capsule to test whether CPP detects the corruption.

units.name: Knowledge Mutation Testing
units.text: Applies mutation testing to governance itself — mutating an applicability condition, invariant, policy priority or baseline generation (or deleting an important rule in sandbox) and checking whether the evaluation suite/Historical Replay detects the degradation.

units.name: Institutional Compression Ratio
units.text: Raw institutional knowledge size ÷ active mission policy size (e.g. 1TB of historical evidence compressed to a perfectly relevant 12KB capsule); the constitution is judged by prevented-failure-per-token/ceremony/complexity, not by rule count.

units.name: Institutional Experience Curves
units.text: Tracks N constructions completed in a task family vs. TTPE; if repeated experience doesn't reduce cost, that triggers a Meta-Incident ("Institutionalization Failure") rather than being excused as "every project is different."

units.name: Mechanism Graph
units.text: Organizes institutional knowledge not by project name but by cross-cutting mechanism categories (Authority, Freshness, Concurrency, Lifecycle, Persistence, Recovery, Observability, Metrology, Representation, Routing, State, Security, Reversibility), with projects as mere provenance nodes.

units.name: Engineering Theorem Prover
units.text: Infers "IF multiple representations of same fact AND writers>1 AND no authority contract THEN divergence risk" from the Mechanism Graph, generating predicted architecture failures before a bug occurs.

units.name: Decision Reopening Engine
units.text: Automatically marks a past decision re-openable when the assumption that justified it changes (e.g. "no ARM support" becomes false after a new library version ships).

units.name: Temporal Decision Graph
units.text: Turns architecture decisions into living nodes with evidence, assumptions, dependencies and reopen conditions rather than dead ADR documents.

units.name: Institutional Self-Hosting
units.text: Applies the entire Institutional State Runtime to CPP's own construction of itself — its bugs feed UDFLL, its architecture mistakes feed KIFS, its human corrections feed HIC, its bottlenecks feed IFC, its reusable discoveries feed UCR, its own baseline feeds UBC.

units.name: Constitutional Planes (Proposal/Evaluation/Ratification/Execution)
units.text: Separates the ability to propose institutional changes (Proposal Plane) from evaluating them against the current constitution (Evaluation Plane), promoting them (Ratification Plane) and executing under the new generation (Execution Plane), preventing self-certification loops.

units.name: CPP Constitutional Kernel
units.text: A small, hard-to-change core of 15-30 invariants (evidence provenance, authority ordering, no-silent-baseline-lowering, reversibility, claim typing, audit trail) beneath which the Institutional State Runtime, UBC Compiler, Capability Packs, Evaluators and Enforcement adapters can evolve freely.

units.name: Seven Planes Architecture
units.text: The full flywheel conceptualized as seven planes (Reality → Evidence → Institutional State → Intelligence → Governance → Compilation → Execution, looping back to Reality) plus an eighth Meta-Institutional Intelligence plane observing the other seven to find what's limiting compounding.
entities: Reality / Evidence / Institutional State / Intelligence / Governance / Compilation / Execution planes; 8th plane = Meta-Institutional Intelligence

units.name: Meta-Flywheel
units.text: Five nested improvement levels: improving software → improving how we learn from software → improving how we institutionalize learning → improving how we choose what to improve → improving how we evaluate that meta-process.

units.name: Institutional Dividend
units.text: Requires every significant construction to leave behind at least one of: new capability, new immunity, new benchmark, new invariant, new instrument, new primitive, negative knowledge, better router, or better evaluator, else effort was consumed without capitalization.

units.name: Capital Allocation Model
units.text: IFC computes marginal institutional return across competing uses of engineering effort (ship product, fix failure, generalize capability, build primitive, improve evaluator, improve tooling, research frontier, reduce complexity) — an explicit capital-allocation model for engineering civilization.

units.name: Universal Engineering Civilization Layer
units.text: The model-independent institutional intelligence layer whose portable outputs (Engineering Capability Package, Failure Immunity Package, Baseline Manifest, Evaluation Suite, Certified Primitive, Production Receipt, Epistemic Certificate) can be consumed by any repo/model/CI/human team without CPP itself, feeding evidence back regardless of which executor produced it.

units.name: Bug Severity Levels L1–L5
units.text: A five-level bug taxonomy: L1 Product Bug (wrong output), L2 Agent Bug (constructor acted wrong), L3 Institutional State Bug (corrupted knowledge/authority), L4 Governance Bug (wrong promotion/rejection), L5 Meta-Learning Bug (the improvement mechanism itself failed to detect it was improving badly) — L5 deemed most dangerous.

units.name: Ultimate Done-Gate
units.text: For a major engineering discovery, "Done" requires product fixed, evidence durable, root cause proven, failure family classified, analogous exposure scanned, regression created, capability extracted, applicability bounded, institutional state updated transactionally, baseline impact assessed, historical replay performed where warranted, future behavior verified, and human rediscovery eliminated — scaled proportionally by UBC/IFC.
